pages.text: The Always-On Intelligence Layer Executive Summary · Voice + Copilot, one unified system Executive Summary An intelligence layer that listens, thinks, and remembers — across every call, every brainstorm, every brand. One system. Two modes of conversation. Built on the memory and orchestration infrastructure Ad Pros already operates — extended so the entire team and every client brand can think with it in real time. The Thesis Your data stack, your client history, your creative library, and your institutional knowledge should be available in the moment you need them — whether you're walking into a pitch, on a live client call, brainstorming a creative angle, or debriefing after a meeting. The interface shouldn't matter. The intelligence should be there. What It Is Two modes. One brain. Most AI tools force a choice: a chatbot you type at, a meeting recorder that reads to you after the fact, a voice assistant that can't access your business. This system collapses them into a single agent with two ways of showing up. 🎙 Mode 1 Voice Conversations Talk to it. Ask questions about any client, campaign, creative test, or performance pattern. Brainstorm strategy hands-free. Prep for calls on the walk to the meeting. It speaks back, pulling from the same memory the entire team writes to. 👁 Mode 2 Silent Call Copilot Sits quietly on live calls — internal, client, pitch, strategy. Listens to both sides. Surfaces relevant context to you visually, never audibly. Recalls the last conversation, the current numbers, the contract terms, the pattern it's seen before. You stay present. It handles the recall. Where It Fits Inside the 8-step model. This is not a new system. It is a new set of inputs and outputs to the intelligence infrastructure already designed in the Ad Pros operating model. Here is exactly where voice + copilot touches each step. 01 Collect Input Layer Voice conversations and live-call audio become two new signal sources — alongside GA4, Shopify, Slack, and CRM. Every spoken interaction is captured and flows upstream. 02 Organize Ingestion Layer The Librarian routes audio signals the same way it routes other inputs — tagged by client, brand, participant, topic, and intent. 03 Remember Context Layer Conversations become permanent memory. BigQuery holds the structured outcomes, pgvector holds the semantic embeddings. Every future conversation can reference every past one. 04 Think Intelligence Layer A new Conversation Agent joins Noor in the intelligence layer. Fast model for real-time listening, Claude for reasoning. Noor routes between them. 05 Plan Planning Layer Insights surfaced during calls and decisions made in voice sessions feed directly into ClickUp and Linear as the plans they become. 06 Assign Delegation Layer "Voice → assign task" and "copilot flag → task" become first-class paths into the same human / AI / hybrid delegation model. 07 Action Execution Layer Work gets done. The conversation that triggered it is linked as context, so the executor knows why — not just what. 08 Review Audit Layer Every conversation becomes auditable. Did the call land? Did the brainstorm ship? Did the copilot's recommendation improve the outcome? Closed loop. Primary insertion points: Steps 1, 3, 4, and 8. The system captures (1), remembers (3), thinks with the team (4), and feeds the audit loop (8). It runs across the whole system rather than living inside any one step — a machine-level capability, consistent with how Noor operates. Who It Serves Built for two audiences. Same system. Ad Pros operates on both sides of the performance marketing relationship. This system is designed to serve both. Agency Side For Ad Pros strategists, media buyers, creative teams, and leadership. The agency runs on conversations — client QBRs, pitch calls, internal pod syncs, creative reviews, retention conversations. Every one of those is a decision moment, and today the context lives in separate heads and scattered tools. Pitch call Prospect mentions a competitor's creative approach. Copilot surfaces competitive intel from your ad library data — no scrambling, no "I'll follow up on that." Client QBR Client asks about a campaign from three months ago. Copilot pulls the performance data, the creative, and the decision rationale from the last QBR deck — all before you finish your sentence. Retention conversation Client signals hesitation. Copilot flags patterns from prior clients who used similar language, with retention plays that worked historically. Between calls Walking between meetings, strategist says: "Prep me for the 47 Skin call in twenty minutes." Voice mode walks through recent performance, open concerns, and the last meeting's follow-ups. Brand Side For DTC founders, ecommerce operators, and in-house marketing teams. Brands live inside their own data — Shopify, Meta Ads, Google Ads, Klaviyo, Triple Whale, Northbeam. The copilot collapses that fragmented stack into one conversational layer. Ask anything. Be prepared for every meeting. Never lose institutional context when someone leaves. Agency review call Founder on a call with their agency. Copilot surfaces real-time performance against targets, flags anomalies in the current spend pattern, and recalls the creative directions agreed to last quarter. Strategic planning Operator asks voice mode: "Which of our top ten SKUs have degraded in ROAS over the last sixty days, and what creative angles did we retire?" Answer in seconds, with sources. Vendor negotiation On a call with a supplier or partner, copilot pulls the contract terms, the historical performance of this relationship, and flags commitments made in prior conversations. Post-meeting debrief Founder leaves a board call. Voice mode: "Walk me through the decisions we just made and draft the follow-up." The conversation is already transcribed, categorized, and ready to action. How It Works The audio-to-action loop. Both modes run the same pipeline. Only the inputs and outputs differ. Capture Voice or Call Audio → Understand Conversation Agent → Retrieve Memory Layer Reason Claude + Noor → Surface Voice or Visual → Write Back Memory + ClickUp Every interaction — voice or copilot — reads from and writes to the same session memory. The system gets smarter about your business every time it's used. Where It Lives Four surfaces. One agent. The same intelligence shows up wherever the conversation is happening. 📱 Mobile Voice App Talk to it anywhere. Prep, brainstorm, query, debrief. Hands-free, context-aware. 💻 Desktop Copilot Overlay Silent sidebar during calls. Insights appear visually. Stays out of the way until relevant. 💬 Slack Integration Continue conversations in Slack. Ask the same questions in text. Same memory, different channel. 📞 Meeting Bot Joins Zoom, Meet, and Teams calls automatically. Captures, categorizes, and remembers. How It Behaves The operating principles. A copilot that speaks out of turn breaks the call. A copilot that never speaks is just a recorder. These principles draw the line. 01 Silent by default on calls Copilot never speaks during live conversations. All output is visual and only to the operator. The call belongs to the humans. 02 Facts before opinions The system surfaces what's known — performance data, contract terms, prior conversations, patterns. Strategic suggestions are rare, reserved for clear signal, and always cite their source. 03 Consent and disclosure first Every call where the copilot is active is disclosed and consented to. For client calls, consent is baked into agreements. Trust is the product. 04 One memory, every interface Ask about last Tuesday's call on your phone while you're walking, and the system answers from the same memory the copilot wrote to during the call. No re-briefing, ever. 05 Scoped to calls that matter Not every call gets the copilot. QBRs, pitches, retention conversations, strategic reviews — yes. Standups and quick syncs — no. The surface area is curated, not maximal. 06 Privacy-first multi-tenant ...

pages.title: BigQuery Access Tradeoffs
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: BigQuery Access Tradeoffs Infrastructure decision memo · Engineering Infrastructure Decision Give the team BigQuery access through Claude — without handing out the keys. Three routes to put Claude between your team and BigQuery, compared on the six dimensions that actually decide the call. Custom web app, MCP server wired into Noor, or off-the-shelf (Hex / Mode / Count). Dimension Custom Web App service account + SSO MCP Server in Noor scoped tools, orchestrator-native Off-the-Shelf Hex / Mode / Count 01 Build effort How long until it ships? Weekend → week One auth layer, one service account, one Claude API wrapper. Straightforward. 2–4 weeks Server + scoped tools + observability + integration into Noor. Biggest lift. Day one Connect BQ, invite team, done. No code. 02 Cost at 26 seats Monthly burn ~$20/mo + API Hosting is negligible. Pay for Anthropic tokens only. ~$20/mo + API Same profile as custom — your dev time is the real cost. $1.5K–3K/mo $50–100+/user/month across the team adds up fast. 03 Access control How surgical can it get? Strong Define allowed queries, tables, and redactions at the app layer. Strongest Tools are the contract. Pod-level RLS, audited per call, reusable everywhere. Workspace-level Fine for most cases; limited if you want per-pod row logic. 04 Stack fit Does it compound? One-off utility Sits alongside Noor but doesn't extend it. Native BQ becomes a tool every future agent (media buyer, CRO, reporting) inherits. Outside the system Lives in a separate product. No compounding. 05 Moat / productization Can it ship to clients? Low Utility. Doesn't ship to clients. High "Ask your data anything" becomes a feature of the agentic offering. None Pure buy. Their moat, not yours. 06 Blast radius What breaks if it breaks? Isolated Only the chat UI is down. Contained failure. Systemic Every dependent agent is affected. Demands real observability and fallbacks. Vendor's problem Their SLA, their on-call. The Call MCP in Noor is the destination. Custom web app is the bridge. Hex is the placeholder — if anything. MCP compounds with everything else being built and becomes part of what gets productized. The custom app is a legitimate 2-week de-risking step before wiring BigQuery into the orchestrator. Off-the-shelf only earns a spot as a 30-day bridge while the real thing is built — never as where we land.

pages.title: BigQuery MCP: Data Team Request
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: BigQuery MCP: Data Team Request Connecting Noor to BigQuery via Google's official MCP server What we're doing Connecting our internal AI assistant (Noor) to BigQuery using Google's official BigQuery MCP server. This replaces the current ad-hoc setup, where a service account JSON sits unencrypted on the Mac Mini Noor runs on with no real query path. The official server is fully managed by Google, runs at https://bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp , authenticates via OAuth 2.0 + IAM, and writes every query to Cloud Audit Logs. No service account keys live on our side. Source: docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp What we need from you 1. Confirm scope Project ID: is ad-pros-2024 the right project for client and campaign data, or should Noor point somewhere else? Datasets in scope: which datasets should Noor be able to query? (e.g. campaign performance, creative analytics, client reporting) Datasets to explicitly exclude: anything with raw PII, billing data, or anything regulated that Noor should never see 2. Provision a dedicated service account Please create a service account just for Noor so we can rotate or revoke it independently: SA name: noor-bq-reader@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com Display name: Noor BigQuery Reader (AdPros AI assistant) 3. Grant three IAM roles, scoped tightly PROJECT=ad-pros-2024 SA=noor-bq-reader@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com # Allow MCP tool calls (project-level) gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT \ --member="serviceAccount:${SA}" \ --role="roles/mcp.toolUser" # Allow running query jobs (project-level) gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT \ --member="serviceAccount:${SA}" \ --role="roles/bigquery.jobUser" # Read access -- apply per dataset, NOT project-wide # Repeat for each dataset Noor should see bq update --source_dataset_access_file - $PROJECT:<dataset_name> <<EOF # add: { "role": "READER", "userByEmail": "${SA}" } EOF (Or grant roles/bigquery.dataViewer per dataset via the console if that's easier.) Important No project-wide dataViewer . We want Noor's read access scoped only to the datasets you explicitly approve. 4. Allow impersonation from one human account So we don't have to ship a key file, grant Service Account Token Creator on the SA to a single human Google identity (probably Nehal or whoever administers Noor on our side). That person runs gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account=... once on the Mac Mini, and ADC handles token refresh from there. No key ever touches disk. gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding $SA \ --member="user:<admin-email>@adpros.com" \ --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator" 5. Cost guardrails (recommended, optional) Two reasonable limits on the SA: Per-query cap: we'll set maximum_bytes_billed = 10 GB as the default in our MCP config so Noor can't accidentally trigger a multi-TB query Daily quota on the SA (if you want a hard ceiling): set a custom BigQuery query usage quota in the GCP console under IAM → Quotas, scoped to this SA What we'll do on our end Wire the MCP server into Noor's agent config Configure ADC with SA impersonation Delete the existing ad-pros-2024-bq-sa.json from disk once the new path is verified Update Noor's internal docs so she knows which datasets exist and how to query them Test from both Telegram and Slack with two authorized users (TG and Nehal) before opening up to the broader team Audit trail you'll get Every query Noor runs will appear in Cloud Audit Logs ( bigquery.googleapis.com ) with: Service account: noor-bq-reader Query SQL Bytes scanned and billed Requester label (we'll inject the originating Slack or Telegram user ID as a query label so you can attribute it) Timeline Whenever fits your team. We're ready on our end as soon as the SA and IAM grants land. Contact TG ( tg@100.partners ) is driving the setup. Reach out with any questions about scope or roles.

pages.text: Frameworks Completed for Ad Pros Each framework filled in — not explained. Master summary in the final tab. Completed Frameworks · Filled In Each framework, run on Ad Pros. Not definitions. Filled-in artifacts. Each tab is one framework completed for "performance partner for 8-figure operators" — using the 2026 deck, the kicker pricing, the Creator Performance Network, the Intelligence Stack, and the Dream Client filter as inputs. The final tab is the master summary. 01 Dunford 5 02 Sales Pitch 03 POV 04 Lightning Strike 05 Magic Triangle 06 Languaging 07 Superconsumers 08 22 Laws 09 Lifecycle 10 JTBD + Chasm 11 Master Summary April Dunford · Obviously Awesome (2019) The five components, completed for Ad Pros. Each component constrains the next. Read top to bottom. 1 Component 01 · Competitive Alternatives What does an 8-figure operator do if Ad Pros doesn't exist? Status quo (the real winner): they keep media in-house with a junior buyer or marketing manager, and accept the variance. This is the default Ad Pros has to beat first. Generic performance agencies (Common Thread, Disruptive, Tier 11, dozens of mid-market shops): flat retainers $5K–$25K/mo, traditional team structure, indifferent to outcomes beyond the contract. Freelance buyer + freelance creative roster: $3K–$8K/mo combined, no integration, all coordination falls on the operator. Fractional CMO + outsourced execution: $10K–$15K/mo for strategy, separate vendors for buying and creative. Higher senior-eyes coverage but no production muscle. Holding-company "growth" arms (WPP/Publicis/Stagwell digital units): expensive, slow, optimized for Fortune-500 not 8-figure DTC. 2 Component 02 · Differentiated Capabilities What does Ad Pros have that none of the alternatives do? CPA-linked variable pricing. $5K base + tiered kicker (4% / 3% / 2% / 1.5%) means Ad Pros gets paid more when the operator wins, less when they don't. No major alternative offers this — they bill flat. Creator Performance Network with 7/3 split. Creators participate in performance economics. Brands buy a creator program where the agency, brand, and creators share upside. No major alternative offers performance-aligned creator economics. The Intelligence Stack (AI Ads Library + Intel + Agentic Workflows / Noor): proprietary AI infrastructure processing 5K+ Meta ads/day, BigQuery + Supabase + Claude API stack. Most agencies have no in-house AI infrastructure — they use third-party SaaS. 9 Dimensions Creative Strategy + Creative Matrix + Breakthrough classification : a named creative scoring system with a breakthrough definition (5–10% of account spend, ROAS target, <90 days). Most agencies score creative ad-hoc. 11 channels managed by one team : Meta, Google, YouTube, AppLovin, TikTok, Native, Snap, Pinterest, CTV, Bing, LinkedIn, Reddit. No fee-per-platform. Most alternatives charge separately per channel or only cover 2–3. Operator-grade case studies at scale : $4M/mo Kachava, $4M+/mo SupportPets revenue, $2M/mo AudienHearing, AG1 / Canada Goose / Infiniwell. Few alternatives have $1M+/mo managed-spend case studies in DTC. 3 Component 03 · Differentiated Value What value do those capabilities deliver to an 8-figure operator? Aligned incentives → lower variance. With CPA-linked pricing the agency earns more when the operator wins. Operators stop fighting the agency to produce more, test faster, scale harder — incentives are already pointing the same direction. Performance creator economics → cheaper, better creator volume. CPN's 7/3 split lets creators earn upside instead of flat fees. This attracts a higher tier of creator at lower cost-per-asset, which compounds creative testing velocity. AI infrastructure → faster breakthrough discovery. The Intelligence Stack means new winners are identified and scaled in days not weeks, and competitive intel is processed continuously not quarterly. Named creative scoring → predictable breakthrough yield. Operators get one breakthrough ad per quarter at a minimum (Foundation tier) up to one per month (Breakthrough tier). Predictable creative ROI, not "we'll try." Multi-channel under one team → no agency tax across channels. 11 channels, one team, one fee. Operators stop paying 3 agencies for 3 channels. Coordination overhead drops to zero. 4 Component 04 · Best-Fit Customer Who cares enough about that value to pay partnership economics? The Dream Client filter from the deck, sharpened for self-selection: $3M+/mo revenue ($250K minimum monthly floor) $1M+/mo paid spend ($100K minimum monthly floor) AOV $50–$150 (mass-market DTC, not luxury, not subscription-only) 30%+ revenue from repeat customers (LTV economics that justify premium fees) Founder-led OR a CEO who personally reviews ad performance weekly Has tried 2+ agencies before and fired them (knows the pain of vendor relationships) Treats ad spend as a P&L line, not a marketing expense Verticals that fit cleanly: health/supplements (Kachava, AG1, Infiniwell), pet (SupportPets), wellness tech (AudienHearing), apparel/lifestyle with strong repeat (Canada Goose). Verticals that don't fit: B2B SaaS, single-purchase products with no repeat (mattresses, furniture), low-AOV ecommerce ($<$50), local services, anything below $500K/mo total spend. 5 Component 05 · Market Category What category context makes the value obvious? Frame Ad Pros inside the existing "performance marketing agency" category — buyers already understand the category and what they expect from it (media buying, creative, reporting). Don't try to invent a new category; the cost of educating the market is too high and the position is sharp enough without it. Claim a sub-position inside that category: "performance partner" — the agency model where fees scale with operator outcomes. This is positioned against "performance vendor" (the default), which most agencies are even when they call themselves partners. The category line: "Performance partner for 8-figure operators." Six words. Audience-first. Self-selecting. Reads like a job description that exists in the market, not a tagline an agency invented. The recursion check Each component reinforces the next. Best-fit customer (8-figure operator with 30%+ repeat revenue) cares about lower variance and faster breakthrough discovery. That value comes from differentiated capabilities (CPA pricing, CPN, Intelligence Stack). Those capabilities only differentiate against the alternatives (status quo, generic agencies, freelancers). All of it lives inside the performance partner sub-category. The framework holds. April Dunford · Sales Pitch (Sales Pitch, 2023) The Ad Pros sales pitch, structured. Dunford's pitch sequence builds on the 5 components. It's the order to walk a prospect through on a discovery call. Step 1 · Insight "Most 8-figure DTC brands have one thing in common: they've fired at least two agencies. The pattern isn't bad agencies — it's misaligned incentives. When the agency gets paid the same whether you scale or stall, the relationship rots." Step 2 · Alternatives + Trade-offs "The four ways operators handle this today: keep it in-house and accept the variance, hire a flat-fee agency, stitch together freelancers, or pay a fractional CMO who outsources execution. Each one trades off something — usually senior eyes for cost, or coordination for control." Step 3 · The Different Approach "There's a fifth option, and it's the one we built. Performance partner economics: low floor, kicker on spend, equity-like exposure for creators. We get paid more when you scale and less when you don't. Same direction, same incentives, no rotting." Step 4 · The Capabilities (proof of different) "Three things make this work. The Breakthrough System: a named creative scoring methodology that produces a quantified breakthrough ad every 30–90 days at 5–10% of account spend. The Creator Performance Network: 7% to us, 3% to creators, performance-aligned. And the Intelligence Stack: proprietary AI infrastructure processing 5,000+ ads a day so we ...

pages.title: TheCinematic AdFactory.
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Ad Pros · Internal System / v1.0 · Apr 2026 / docs.adpros.com/cinematic-factory The Cinematic Ad Factory. An autonomous agent system that transforms any e-commerce brand brief into a 15–30 second cinematic hero spot — engineered for direct response, art-directed for virality. Built on a deconstructed library of 30+ viral references, six genre archetypes, and three narrative structures the system selects per brand fit. 8 Production Agents 6 Genre Archetypes 3 Narrative Structures 72h Brief → Hero Spot 01 Overview 02 Frameworks 03 Genre Library 04 Cinematic Beats 05 Variable Schema 06 Agent System 07 Prompt Stack 08 Intake Tiers 09 Quality & DR 10 Viral Variables 11 SOP 12 Roadmap 01 · Overview Brief in. Cinema out. Most "AI ads" look like AI ads. The Cinematic Factory exists to do the opposite — to produce single 15–30 second hero spots that feel like they came out of a real production house, but cost a fraction and ship in days. This is the operating manual. The core thesis. Cinema is reproducible. Every viral cinematic ad — Apple's "Shot on iPhone," Liquid Death's "Plastic Demon," Nike's hero pieces, Old Spice's surreal sketches — is built from the same finite library of beats, lenses, pacing decisions, and emotional arcs. We've deconstructed that library into a structured variable schema. The Factory takes a brand brief, selects the right genre and structure based on product fit, fills the variables, and runs an 8-agent production pipeline end-to-end. The promise A DTC brand provides a brief. 72 hours later , they receive a single 15–30s cinematic hero spot that meets a measurable DR floor (CTR, hook rate, hold rate) and a viral ceiling (saves, shares, watch-through). Same system. Any brand. Any product category. What this is not. Not a UGC factory. UGC has its own pipeline. This is for hero, brand-defining, top-of-funnel cinematic. Not a 30-variant test pack. One spot per brief. Optimized to be the best single ad they could run, not the most ads they could run. Not generic AI footage stitched together. Every shot is composed, color-graded, and edited against a structured beat sheet. Not a replacement for live action when live action is the right call. The system flags when a brief needs hybrid or live action and routes accordingly. How it fits the Ad Pros stack. The Factory plugs into the existing 8-step intelligence flow — Collect → Organize → Remember → Think → Plan → Assign → Review → Improve — the same backbone that powers Workflow Factory and the Always-On Intelligence Layer. Brand briefs land in Collect , get structured into the variable schema in Organize , are matched against the reference library in Remember , scripted and storyboarded in Think , scheduled across the production pipeline in Plan , executed by the 8 agents in Assign , gated through Eval in Review , and fed back into the library in Improve . Operating tenets. TENET 01 Cinema is structured . Every cinematic ad is reducible to a schema: hook archetype, narrative structure, genre, beat sequence, lens grammar, color palette, sound design, payoff type. We treat the schema as the product. TENET 02 DR floor is non-negotiable. The spot has to make money. Hook rate, hold rate, CTR, and CAC are measured before any subjective judgment is applied. If it's beautiful but doesn't convert, it's killed. TENET 03 Genre is diagnostic , not stylistic. The Recommender agent picks genre based on category, audience, and product physics — not founder vibes. A supplement brand might map to Liquid Death; an oat milk to A24. Fit beats taste. TENET 04 Every shot is load-bearing . 15–30 seconds is brutal. There are no transition shots. Every frame must do narrative, sensory, brand, or DR work — usually two of those at once. The beat sheet enforces this. TENET 05 Library compounds. Every spot we ship gets evaluated, tagged, and added to the reference library — winning patterns get weighted up, losers get weighted down. The Factory gets sharper with every brief. TENET 06 Humans gate the three moments . Brand approval after the brief, creative approval after the storyboard, final approval before deploy. Everything else is automated. Three gates, no more, no less. 02 · Frameworks Three narrative structures. Every cinematic spot the Factory produces is built on one of three structural skeletons. The Recommender agent picks based on product type, hero claim, and audience awareness level. These aren't templates — they're load-bearing scaffolds that the genre, beats, and visual grammar hang off of. Structure 01 · Hook–Tension–Reveal–CTA The DR-weighted skeleton. Best for products where the buyer needs to be re-educated about a problem they didn't know they had, or a category they thought they understood. Use when: product is differentiated by a single sharp claim, audience is cold, conversion is measured in clicks not lift. 0–2s Hook 2–6s Tension 6–12s Stakes 12–18s Reveal 18–22s Proof 22–26s Hero Shot 26–28s CTA 28–30s Brand Structure 02 · Cold Open → Transformation → Reveal → Brand The cinema-first skeleton. Best for products where the experience of using the product is itself the story — supplements, beverages, skincare, wearables, anything where there's a felt before/after. Use when: the product produces a state change the audience can feel through the screen. 0–3s Cold Open 3–7s Before State 7–11s Catalyst 11–17s Transform 17–22s After State 22–25s Product Reveal 25–28s Brand World 28–30s CTA Stamp Structure 03 · Character → Conflict → Product as Resolution The story-first skeleton. Best for brands with a strong founder narrative or where the customer is the hero of the story — coaching, performance gear, niche health tech, anything where buying is identity-aligning. Use when: the audience needs to see themselves in the spot before they'll buy. 0–3s Character In 3–8s World 8–13s Conflict 13–18s Crisis 18–22s Product Enters 22–26s Resolution 26–28s New State 28–30s Brand & CTA How the Recommender picks. Signal Hook–Tension–Reveal Transformation Character–Conflict Audience awareness Cold / problem-unaware Solution-aware Most-aware / loyal Product type Sharp single claim State-change product Identity-aligned Hero claim format Number / contrast Sensation / outcome Belief / philosophy DR weighting Highest Medium Lower (lifetime value) Default genre fit Liquid Death · Old Spice Apple · A24 Nike · Documentary 03 · Genre Library Six cinematic archetypes. Genre is the visual and tonal grammar the Factory dresses the chosen narrative structure in. Each archetype carries its own lens choices, color palette, pacing rules, music genre, and shot library. The Recommender selects one primary and one secondary genre per brief — most spots blend two for differentiation. Reference · Apple, Aesop, Loro Piana Luxury Minimal Slow, premium, deliberate. Negative space as the loudest design choice. Product as artifact. 85mm · 24fps · macro · cool whites · ambient pad · 8–12 cuts Reference · Nike, Hoka, Lululemon hero Athletic Hero Kinetic, emotional, maximalist. Sweeping movement, voiceover-led, the customer as protagonist. 35mm · 60fps · handheld · warm contrast · cinematic score · 18–24 cuts Reference · Liquid Death, Loop Earplugs, Magic Spoon Disruptor Absurd Irreverent, attention-hijacking, cinematically over-produced jokes. Treats DTC like indie film. 28mm · 24fps · saturated · synth · whip-pans · 14–20 cuts Reference · A24 trailers, Equinox, Mubi Atmospheric Mood Moody, character-driven, slow-burn cinema. Often dialogue-light. Product as object in a world. 50mm · 24fps · low-key · grain · ambient drone · 6–10 cuts Reference · Old Spice, Dr Squatch, Skittles CGI Maximalist Surreal, hyper-stylized, joke-as-set-piece. AI-generated worlds where physics negotiates. wide · 30fps · hyper-saturated · funk · 20+ cuts Reference · Patagonia, Allbirds, Athletic Greens founder Documentary Founder Authentic, talking-head + b-roll, founder as protagonist. Earned credibility as the hook. 35mm · 24fps · natural light · sync sound · 10–14 ...

pages.title: Alternatives to Claude Managed Agents
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Alternatives to Claude Managed Agents Infrastructure decision brief · v3 · full landscape 01 Executive Summary 02 For Ad Pros 03 Full Landscape 04 Feature Breakdown 05 42 Decision Questions 06 Cost Modeling 07 Migration Risk 01 · Executive Summary How to choose Claude Managed Agents (CMA) is a hosted agent harness — sandboxing, sessions, memory, tool execution, and tracing, all run by Anthropic for $0.08/session-hour plus tokens. The alternatives split along two axes: who runs the infrastructure , and which models you can use . The right choice depends on lock-in tolerance, scale, and how much of the moat lives inside the agent's memory. The decision in one sentence If your moat is memory and learning loops, own the harness. If your moat is the agent's task quality and you want to ship fast, let Anthropic run it. MENTAL MODEL · THREE LAYERS Most agent stacks have three distinct layers. Conflating them is how teams end up paying three vendors for one problem: LOOP — the agent code itself: prompts, tools, control flow. Mastra · Vercel AI SDK · Claude Agent SDK · OpenAI Agents SDK · LangGraph · CrewAI RUNTIME — durable execution: scheduling, retries, surviving disconnects. CMA · Cloudflare Agents · Inngest · Temporal · Trigger.dev · Vercel Workflows SANDBOX — code execution isolation: where agent-written code actually runs. E2B · Modal · Daytona · Blaxel · Vercel Sandbox · Cloudflare Sandbox Hosted platforms (CMA, Cloudflare Agents, Bedrock AgentCore) bundle all three. SDKs let you mix and match. Choose based on which layer you actually need to control. The five buckets A Hosted, model-locked CMA (Claude), Salesforce Agentforce (CRM-locked). Fastest to ship, deepest tuning, highest lock-in. B Hosted, model-agnostic Cloudflare Agents (Think), Bedrock AgentCore, Microsoft Foundry, Google Vertex AI Agent Builder, OpenAI Agents SDK. Someone else runs the infra, models stay swappable. Cloudflare's hibernation pricing (free when idle) is the breakthrough. C SDK / library, you deploy Claude Agent SDK, Mastra (TS), Vercel AI SDK, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen. Full control over deployment. Engineering cost but no per-session platform fee. Mastra is the rising TypeScript-native option. D Self-hosted OSS OpenClaw, Multica, Cabinet, Eigent. Maximum control, zero lock-in, full ops cost on your team. E Workflow / no-code n8n, Dust, Relevance AI, Decagon. Visual builder, business-team-friendly, less custom logic but faster to deploy for standard workflows. Three things people miss i. Memory = lock-in Models are easy to swap. Once agents have written months of memory into a proprietary store, switching costs explode. ii. $0.08/hr scales One agent for an hour is a rounding error. 500 agents running concurrently is $40/hr just for the harness, on top of tokens. iii. Infra is consolidating OpenAI, Anthropic, and Cloudflare are all bundling sandbox + memory + harness. Standalone primitives (E2B, Pinecone) are commoditizing fast. Pick by primary constraint SPEED TO PRODUCTION Claude Managed Agents MULTI-MODEL FLEXIBILITY Cloudflare Agents / Mastra / OpenAI Agents SDK COST AT SCALE / IDLE-HEAVY Cloudflare Agents · pay only when active TYPESCRIPT-FIRST TEAM Mastra (batteries-included) or Vercel AI SDK (minimal) ZERO LOCK-IN / DATA RESIDENCY OpenClaw or Multica ALREADY ON AWS / AZURE / GCP Bedrock AgentCore / Foundry / Vertex CRM-CENTRIC WORKFLOWS Salesforce Agentforce YOUR STACK TODAY Claude Agent SDK + Supabase 02 · Recommendations for Ad Pros Mapped to what you're actually building Based on the current Ad Pros AI stack — Noor (ClickUp + BigQuery + Supabase + Claude API), the 8-agent Workflow Factory, the Media Intelligence Pipeline processing ~5K Meta ads/day, and the AI twin video pipeline — here's how the alternatives map to specific projects. RECOMMENDED PRIMARY · NOOR / WORKFLOW FACTORY Claude Agent SDK + your existing stack Noor is already built on ClickUp, BigQuery, Supabase, and the Claude API. The Agent SDK formalizes what you have — agent loop, tool execution, context compaction — without forcing you onto Anthropic's hosted runtime. Keep Supabase as the memory store, BigQuery as the data layer, and skip session-hour fees on agents that run constantly. Why Your moat is the data layer + workflow logic, not the harness Cost vs CMA Save ~$60/mo per agent running 24/7 ($0.08 × 730 hr) Risk You own ops, but you're already running prod infra USE FOR · MEDIA INTELLIGENCE PIPELINE Stay on Anthropic Batch API Don't move the ~5K ads/day pipeline to CMA. Batch API is 50% cheaper for high-volume async work, and you're not running a long-horizon agent — it's a stateless classification pipeline at scale. CMA's value is sessions and memory; you don't need either here. Use CMA only for: the QA audit agent that reasons across full classification output. WORTH PILOTING · CLIENT-FACING (FUTURE) Claude Managed Agents If Noor ever gets productized for clients (white-label agent infra for DTC brands), CMA's sandboxing, scoped permissions, and identity isolation are exactly what would otherwise take 3 months to build. Single-tenant per-client agents with session-hour pricing maps cleanly to client billing. Why: multi-tenant security is the hardest part to build correctly. STRONG CONTENDER · MULTI-AGENT WORKLOADS Cloudflare Agents (Think) The most interesting alternative for your stack. Each agent is a Durable Object with its own SQLite — millions of agents possible, free when idle (hibernation), pay only for CPU time when active. Model-agnostic via AI Gateway (14+ providers including Anthropic). Sandbox SDK + Dynamic Workers handle code execution. If you ever need 1 agent per client × 5 clients × 20 agents running mostly idle, this pricing model crushes CMA's session-hour fee. Trade-off: TypeScript-first, requires Cloudflare Workers mental model. Best if a team member already knows the platform. WATCH, DON'T ADOPT · MULTI-MODEL Deep Agents Deploy (LangChain) Useful insurance against Anthropic pricing or capability shifts, but not needed today — Claude is the default and it's working. Re-evaluate if a specific agent ever benefits from Gemini's long context or a local model for cost/privacy. Trigger to revisit: Claude pricing increase, or vertical where Gemini's context window matters. SKIP · NOT YOUR STACK Bedrock AgentCore Only makes sense if you were already on AWS. Adds vCPU-hour + GB-hour pricing complexity, AWS IAM overhead, and a second cloud to manage. You're on Supabase + Cloudflare R2 — staying there is correct. SKIP · TEAM SIZE Self-hosted OpenClaw / Multica Right answer for a 200-person org with a platform team. At ~26 people with most engineering effort going into the products themselves, the ops burden of self-hosting an agent runtime is a tax you don't need to pay yet. SUMMARY Three patterns, not eight Document the harness boundary clearly: which agents call CMA, which call the Agent SDK directly, which use Batch API. Three patterns is fine; eight is chaos. SUGGESTED NEXT 30 DAYS 01. Audit current Noor agents → which actually need long-running sessions vs. one-shot calls? Most don't. 02. Pick one agent to pilot on CMA. The QA audit pipeline or a competitive intel deep-research agent are good candidates. 03. Keep Supabase as the source-of-truth memory store regardless of harness. Don't let agent memory get trapped in any vendor. 04. Document the harness boundary so the team knows when to reach for CMA vs. SDK vs. Batch API. 03 · Full Landscape Every major player, by category The agent infrastructure space is bigger than CMA vs. its direct competitors. There are three layers — loop , runtime , and sandbox — and choosing across all three matters more than which single bundled platform wins. Layer 1 · Hosted Agent Platforms Bundled solutions: harness + runtime + sandbox + memory in one product. ANTHROPIC Claude Managed Agents Claude-native, sessions, memory, dreaming preview. $0.08/sess-hr. CLOUDFLARE Cloudflare Agents (Think) Durable Objects, hibernation pricing, ...

pages.text: Daily Competitor Analysis Agent — SOP Input contract, processing rules, and output template Internal SOP · v1 Daily Competitor Analysis Agent A standard operating procedure for the daily competitive intelligence brief. Surfaces only meaningful changes from competitor ad library activity in the last 24 hours. Read on mobile in 60 seconds. Every line passes the test: would a reader know something they couldn't have guessed? Contents 1. Purpose 2. Input contract 3. Tiering rules 4. Suppression rules 5. Phrasing rules 6. Escalation triggers 7. Output template 8. Sample — active day 9. Sample — quiet day 10. Tone rules 1 Purpose Produce a daily competitive intelligence brief for Ad Pros leadership that surfaces only meaningful changes from competitor ad activity in the last 24 hours. The brief is read on mobile in 60 seconds. The test: every line in the output must pass — would a reader know something they couldn't have guessed? If not, omit the line. Never write "stable," "no changes," "none," or similar non-statements. 2 Input contract The agent receives a JSON payload each morning with this structure per tracked brand. Required fields per brand: name , status , vitals . All other dimensions optional — if absent, agent treats as "no signal." Blocked or no-data brands appear in the LOW section with a single-line status only. { "report_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "tracked_brands": ["Obvi", "Anouk", "Bloom Nutrition", "Ritual", "FC Racing"], "ad_pros_creator_network": ["@handle1", "@handle2", ...], "brands": [ { "name": "Obvi", "status": "active", // "active" | "blocked" | "no_data" "vitals": { "new_ads_24h": 5, "ads_off_24h": 12, "total_running": 47, "total_running_yesterday": 54 }, "days_active": { "buckets": { "lt_7d": 18, "d7_14": 14, "d14_30": 9, "d30_plus": 6 }, "ads_off_by_bucket": { "lt_7d": 8, "d7_14": 0, "d14_30": 4, "d30_plus": 0 }, "days_since_last_winner": 3, "top5_impression_share": 0.62, "top5_impression_share_last_week": 0.45 }, "format_mix": { "current": { "static": 0.22, "video": 0.73, "carousel": 0.05 }, "last_week": { "static": 0.45, "video": 0.50, "carousel": 0.05 } }, "cadence": { "launches_today": 5, "rolling_7d_avg": 1.8 }, "offers": { "new_offers": [{ "offer": "Buy 2 Get 1 Free", "product": "Collagenic Burn", "ad_count": 3 }], "discontinued_offers": [{ "offer": "25% off site-wide" }], "discount_depth_change": null }, "creative": { "new_hooks": ["Selling out fast", "Back in stock — 48hrs only", ...], "new_headlines": ["Lose the bloat, not the muscle"], "new_descriptions": [...] }, "messaging_themes": { "current_top3": ["scarcity", "transformation", "social_proof"], "previous_top3": ["social_proof", "transformation", "ingredient_education"], "entered_top3": ["scarcity"], "dropped_from_top3": ["ingredient_education"] }, "landing_pages": { "new_lps": [], "modified_lps": [{ "url": "...", "change": "added countdown timer" }] }, "whitelisting": { "new_partners": [ { "handle": "@ferrari_lifestyle_mx", "followers": 1200000, "tier": "macro" } ], "removed_partners": [], "ad_pros_network_overlap": [] }, "language": { "current_distribution": { "en": 1.0 }, "yesterday_distribution": { "en": 1.0 }, "new_languages": [] }, "competitor_callouts": { "brands_named": ["AG1"], "ad_count": 1, "days_since_last_callout": 90 } } ] } 3 Tiering rules Assign each brand to one of three tiers based on how many new ads they launched in the last 24h . Volume is the primary signal — everything else (offers, messaging, whitelisting) is detail layered on top. Tier Threshold (new ads launched in 24h) 🔴 High 10+ new ads launched 🟡 Medium 5–10 new ads launched ⚪ Low <5 new ads launched. Includes blocked and no-data brands. 4 Suppression rules per dimension Each dimension is shown only if its trigger fires. Otherwise omit the line entirely. Dimension Show when Vitals row Always — this is the pulse check Cadence >2x or <0.3x of 7-day rolling avg Days-active signal ≥1 ad with 30d+ active turned off, OR >50% of library is <7d old, OR >14 days since last ad crossed 14d active, OR top-5 impression share shifted >15 points week-over-week Format shift Any single format moved >10 points week-over-week Offers New offer launched, OR discount depth changed ≥10 points, OR new discount mechanic Messaging shift New theme entered top 3, OR existing theme dropped from top 3 Hooks ≥3 new hooks, OR new hook represents thematic shift Headlines Net-new positioning angle (not a variation) Landing pages Any new LP, OR existing LP materially modified Whitelisting 🚨 Any newly detected partner. Always flag Ad Pros Creator Network overlaps. Language New language detected, OR distribution shifted >20 points Direct callouts 🚨 Always shown when present. Note ad count and days since last callout. 5 Phrasing rules for surfaced dimensions Days-active signals — plain-language observations, not bucket counts. Example: "4 ads with 14-30d active turned off — killing maturing creatives, not just tests." Format shifts — include before → after percentages. Example: "Static 45% → 22%, Video 50% → 73%." Cadence — include the multiplier vs. avg. Example: "5 launches vs. 1.8/day avg — 2.8x normal velocity." Messaging shifts — say what replaced what. Example: "Scarcity replaces social proof as dominant angle." Whitelisting — include follower tier (micro <100k / mid 100k–1M / macro 1M+). Flag Ad Pros Creator Network overlap with 🚨🚨. pages.title: Framework Recommendations
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Framework Recommendations Service-by-service implications of 'Performance partner for 8-figure operators' Service Architecture Audit If "performance partner for 8-figure operators" is true, this is what changes. Reviewing the 2026 Ad Pros service deck against the positioning. The services are right. The architecture, pricing weight, and naming need surgery. Each tab below covers one service through the framework lens — what stays, what moves, what the position demands. 01 Diagnosis 02 Creative Strategy 03 Creative Production 04 CPN 05 Media Buying 06 AI / Intel / Agentic 07 Dream Client 08 Proposal Math 09 Languaging 10 30-Day Actions The deck is built for vendors. The position is partner. The 2026 deck reads like a service menu — Creative Strategy, Creative Production, CPN, Media Buying, three products coming soon. That's what a competent agency would build. The problem is it's also what every competent agency has built. None of it is wrong. None of it is unique to "performance partner for 8-figure operators" either. Three structural issues surface immediately when read through the framework lens. Issue 1: The fee architecture says vendor In the sample proposal, total fees are $24,060/month against $284K monthly spend — about 8.5% of spend. Of that, only $8,860 (37%) is variable. The other 63% is fixed. A real performance partner would invert that ratio: fixed should cover floor cost, variable should be the dominant component. Right now the kicker is the garnish, not the entrée. Issue 2: The service language is feature-led, not outcome-led "Creative Strategy," "Creative Production," "Media Buying" are the same three nouns 200 other agencies use. None of them name a partnership outcome. None of them filter for 8-figure operators. The deck would read identically if the target client were a $500K/year shop. Issue 3: The "coming soon" trio is buried AI Ads Library, Intel, and Agentic Workflows are the actual category-claim assets — proprietary AI infrastructure most agencies don't have. They're listed last and labeled "coming soon," which signals "side project" rather than "the thing that makes us different." Pirates' Languaging Law: the words you use shape the category. "Coming soon" is the wrong frame for the strongest assets. The honest read The deck wins deals against weaker agencies. It does not yet win deals against better-positioned agencies. The fix is not to add more services. The fix is to restructure how the existing services are priced, named, and sequenced so they live up to the position. The next eight tabs walk service-by-service through the same diagnosis: where it stands today, what each framework demands, and what changes. Creative Strategy: rename it. The deliverable is the asset. Tiers are $5K / $10K / $20K monthly. Deliverables include 22 named items — brand audit, 9 creative dimensions, 90-day roadmap, monthly memo, briefs, scorecards, QBRs. Through the framework lens Dunford on differentiated capabilities: the 9 Dimensions framework, the Creative Matrix, the Breakthrough classification (Loser / Winner / Breakthrough at 5% / 10%) are real differentiated capabilities. Most agencies don't have a named scoring system. This is the most defensible piece of the entire offering. But it's listed as deliverable #4 of 22, not as the hero. Pirates' Languaging: "Creative Strategy" is generic noun-pair. Every agency claims it. The actual differentiated thing is the system — call it that. "The Breakthrough System." "The 9 Dimensions Engine." "Creative Performance Operations." Whatever the name, it should be the same name across the deck, the website, the IG bio, and Slack. Play Bigger's POV: the underlying point of view is "creative is the largest unmanaged variable in performance, and most agencies are flying blind because they don't have a scoring system." That POV is implicit in the deck but never stated. Stating it once would do more work than 22 deliverable bullets. From / to CURRENT "Creative Strategy" 22 deliverables, three tiers by brief volume (20 / 40 / 80), no named system, brand audit listed first. RECOMMENDED "The Breakthrough System" One named system. 9 Dimensions + Creative Matrix + Breakthrough classification stated as the methodology. Tiers measured by breakthroughs produced, not briefs delivered. Recommendation Strategy tier Rename the service. Lead with the system, not the deliverable count. Restructure tiers: Foundation ($5K) is "diagnostic + monthly system review." Accelerator ($10K) is "active management + 1 breakthrough target/quarter." Breakthrough ($20K) is "active management + 1 breakthrough target/month + creative R&D allocation." Tie tier value to outcomes the operator actually buys, not deliverable inventory. Framework call Dunford's "differentiated value" step demands you state the value, not the feature. "20 briefs/month" is a feature. "1 breakthrough ad/month at 5-10% account spend" is a value. The PDF already defines breakthrough on slide 11 — promote that definition into the pricing structure. Creative Production: this is the commodity tier. Tiers are $4K / $8K / $16K monthly for 20 / 40 / 80 concepts. UGC recruiting, post-production, ad spy tools, AI UGC, copywriting, DAM. Through the framework lens Dunford on competitive alternatives: the real alternative isn't another agency's production team. It's the in-house creative team the operator already has, plus a freelance UGC roster, plus their existing post-production vendor. Those alternatives are cheaper . Production at this tier is hard to differentiate on — the work is largely commoditized, and AI is compressing margins fast. Pirates' Magic Triangle: production is product-design work. It needs to fit the category. The category is "performance partner" — meaning every concept produced should be tagged to a hypothesis the strategy tier defined and a result the media buying tier will measure. Production in isolation is a vendor service. Production wired into a closed loop is a partner service. Play Bigger's POV-product fit: production volume alone (80 concepts/month at the top tier) is a quantity claim. A category-king claim would be production volume tied to breakthrough yield — "we ship 80 concepts/month, we expect 4 breakthroughs minimum, and our Creative Matrix shows you exactly which dimensions we're testing." The honest tension Production is the service most exposed to AI commoditization in the next 24 months. The strategic move is not to make production look more premium. It's to position production as the execution arm of the Breakthrough System — so the operator buys the system and production is the throughput of it. If production stands alone, the price ceiling is set by what AI tools cost. Recommendation Production tier Stop selling production as a standalone tier. Bundle it with Creative Strategy. The new top-of-deck offer is "The Breakthrough System: strategy + production + breakthrough guarantee." Production volume becomes a delivery parameter, not a pricing axis. Operators stop comparing $4K-$16K production tiers against freelance rosters and start buying the system. Framework call Pirates' Magic Triangle: product-category fit means the product (production) must serve the category (performance partnership). Standalone production breaks the triangle because it's purchasable as a vendor service. Bundled production reinforces it. Creator Performance Network: this is the category claim. Listed in the deck as "Coming Soon." The 8 deliverables include high-level strategy, creator video production, post-production, UGC management, recruiting, compliance, AI-generated content, and multi-channel distribution. Through the framework lens Pirates' Different Law: CPN is the only service in the deck that no major competitor offers in the same form. The 7/3 split (Ad Pros keeps 7% of spend on creator content, 3% passes to creators) is structural, not tactical. It changes what creators get paid for (performance, not deliverables) and what brands buy (creator ...

pages.text: Free Strategy Call Book a 30-minute growth audit with a senior Ad Pros strategist. Free 30-min growth audit Scale past $1M/month in paid acquisition. We'll build the engine. Book a free 30-minute growth audit. A senior strategist will pressure-test where your ad spend is leaking and map a 90-day plan to scale Meta, Google, TikTok, and AppLovin without burning ROAS. Book my free audit → No pitch. No deck. A working session. $250M+ Generated for clients 85% Avg ROAS 11 Ad channels managed 10+ yrs Performance experience 01 WHY THIS CALL Reading a case study doesn't move ROAS. Implementation does. You already know the levers — creative volume, audience structure, bid strategy, attribution. The gap isn't knowledge. The gap is dialing all of it in for your offer, your margins, and your channel mix at the same time. That's what this audit is for. In 30 minutes a senior strategist will: 1 Pinpoint the single biggest spend leak in your account Audience overlap, creative fatigue, attribution drift, structural inefficiency — we'll name the largest dollar-impact issue in your current setup and quantify it. 2 Map a 90-day scale plan across Meta, Google, TikTok, AppLovin Channel sequencing, creative cadence, budget allocation. Tied to a specific revenue or ROAS target, not a vague "let's grow." 3 Build a creative testing roadmap calibrated to your offer Concept volume, hook variants, format diversification. Output is a 30-day creative brief you can run with us — or with your in-house team. If we're a fit, we'll tell you. If we're not, you walk out with a plan you can run yourself. Either way the call produces work product. 02 BOOK THE AUDIT Pick a time. 30 minutes. One of our senior strategists. A real working session — not a discovery call. Calendar embed lives here in production. Replace with the inline scheduler when this page goes to a paid traffic source. Email book@adpros.com → 03 RESULTS Real brands. Real revenue. Real timelines. Every outcome below came from the same combination of media buying, creative production, and data infrastructure we'll map for you on the call. DTC SUPPLEMENTS $0 → $4.2M Revenue, 6 months. No incremental ad spend after month 2. SKINCARE 2.1x → 3.4x Blended ROAS lift, 90 days. Driven by creative cadence overhaul. CONSUMABLES $1.2M → $3.8M Monthly Meta spend, 12 months. CPA held flat. APPAREL $2M → $2M Same spend. 47% revenue lift via AppLovin expansion. HEALTH $30 → $18 CPA, 60 days. Audience structure rebuild. HOME GOODS $500K → $1.6M Monthly revenue, 4 months. Creative volume 5x. Sample outcomes from the Ad Pros portfolio. Specific brand attribution available under NDA on the call. 04 FIT Who this is for. This call is for you if… You run a DTC or ecommerce brand at $1M+ annual revenue. You're spending $50K+/month on paid acquisition across at least one major channel. You want to scale past your current ceiling without breaking unit economics. You'd benefit from an outside read on creative, media buying, or attribution. You'd consider an outcome-based fee structure tied to performance. This call is NOT for you if… You're pre-revenue or pre-product-market fit. You're spending under $50K/month on paid and aren't ready to commit to a real budget. You want to micromanage tactical decisions inside the ad account. You're shopping for the lowest-cost media buyer. You expect outsized results with no creative or strategic input from your side. 05 RISK The performance fee structure. Our fees scale with your CPA. Hit the target, we earn. Miss the target, our variable fee compresses. Skin in the game on both sides. The full model is published at docs.adpros.com/performance-pricing-model-v2 . We'll walk you through it on the call and tell you whether your account is a fit. 06 COMMON QUESTIONS Frequently asked. Is this a sales pitch? No. The 30 minutes are spent on your account, your numbers, and your bottleneck. We produce a real plan in the call. If we think we're a fit to run it for you, we'll tell you at the end. If we're not, we'll tell you that too. Do you only work with certain verticals? We specialize in DTC and ecommerce — supplements, beauty, apparel, consumables, home goods, health. If your brand is outside ecommerce we'll say so on the call. What's the minimum commitment if we work together? 90 days is the typical first commitment — long enough to rebuild creative cadence, restructure the buy, and read clean attribution. We'll walk you through pricing and structure on the call. Do you charge a flat retainer or a percentage of spend? We use a base retainer plus a variable performance fee tied to a CPA target. The full structure is documented in the performance pricing model linked above. Can we start with a single channel? Yes. Most engagements start with the channel that's biggest or most broken, then expand. We'll map the sequence on the call. What do you actually do in-house? Media buying across 11 paid channels, creative production at scale, data infrastructure (BigQuery, Northbeam, Triple Whale), and a Creative Advisory Board for strategic direction. Roughly 26 people organized into client pods. You've read the page. Now book the call. 30 minutes. A senior strategist. A real plan you walk away with. No pitch. Book my free audit → No obligation. Senior strategist. Real plan delivered on the call.

pages.text: Growth Marketers Role Changes — May 2026 Internal What's Changing Your Role AI & Automation What's Coming The Growth Marketer role is changing. Here's how our updated services and agency model change your role. What's Different You're running client meetings Ownership Growth Strategists have shared the client-facing load on meetings. Going forward, you run your client calls — setting the agenda, presenting performance, and owning the follow-through. The Growth Strategist role is being wound down Structure As the team transitions, strategic ownership shifts more directly to Growth Marketers. For clients you currently share with a Growth Strategist, that collaboration continues as normal. For new clients going forward, you're the primary owner from day one. Client capacity is increasing Capacity Capacity is measured in platforms, not just clients — and the target is 20 Tier 1 platforms or 10 Tier 2 platforms per Growth Marketer. The AI systems being built are specifically designed to make this realistic. A CRO department is being built Coming Soon We're actively hiring for a dedicated CRO role. When it's live, you'll brief CRO the same way you brief the Creative Team — with data and a specific ask. It expands what you can deliver for clients without adding to your execution load. Client meetings are moving to bi-weekly Cadence Weekly client calls are being phased out in favour of bi-weekly. Less time in recurring meetings means more time for analysis, testing, and actual execution. AI is being integrated across your workflow Systems Reporting, analysis, meeting prep, presentations, performance alerts — these are being automated. The goal is to return enough time that higher client capacity becomes operational, not just theoretical. What you own. With more strategic ownership comes clearer accountability. Here's how the role is defined. Core Responsibilities Client Relationship You are the primary point of contact for your clients. The client experience — communication, expectations, escalation — is yours to manage. Testing Methodology You run the testing engine. What gets tested, in what order, with what hypothesis and budget allocation. Scaling Decisions You decide when to scale and when to pull back. Spend decisions within your portfolio are yours to make. Strategic Prioritization You determine what matters most for each client at any given time — what to push on, what to hold, and what to escalate. How You Work with the Creative Team Creative strategy is the Creative Team's domain. Your role is to be the performance layer that informs their decisions. → Surface what's working, what's failing, and what needs a refresh — with data behind it → The Creative Team responds with concept direction, brief guidance, and creative strategy → You need to understand creative strategy well enough to contextualize results for clients, ask the right questions, and flag when something isn't landing Capacity Model Capacity is measured in platforms , not clients. Tiers are based on monthly ad spend per platform. Tier Definitions — Per Platform Tier 1 <$100k/mo Tier 2 $100k–$300k Tier 3 $300k–$1mm Tier 4 $1mm+ Example: A client spending $300k on Meta (Tier 2) + $100k on Google (Tier 1) + $100k on TikTok (Tier 1) = 3 platforms across 2 tiers Goal 1 20 Tier 1 platforms Lower spend per platform, higher volume of accounts Goal 2 10 Tier 2 platforms Higher spend per platform, deeper per-account involvement AI & Automation Higher capacity is only viable if the manual load drops. Reporting, analysis, meeting prep, alerts — these are being automated. AI Systems Roadmap Planned Weekly Internal Performance Report Automated per-client weekly report surfaced internally. Replaces manual data pulling and deck building for internal review. Planned Client Meeting Notes Builder Automatically generates structured meeting notes from call transcripts — action items, decisions, follow-ups, organized and ready. Planned Meeting Prep Builder Pre-call brief generated before each client meeting — recent performance, trends, open items, suggested talking points. In Progress Client Presentation Generator Automatically generates client-facing presentations using account data, onboarding context, and defined templates. Onboarding deck automation is already live. Planned AI Performance Analyst Conversational analysis of account performance. Ask it anything about a client's data — it queries and responds with charts, breakdowns, and follow-up suggestions. Planned Account Audit Tool Structured account audit on demand — surfaces structural issues, budget misallocation, creative gaps, and targeting problems against defined benchmarks. Planned Strategy Document Builder Generates client-specific strategy documents using account history, onboarding data, and performance trends. In Progress Per-Client Slack Alert Channels Every client gets a dedicated Slack channel receiving automated performance alerts. You choose which alerts matter most per client based on current goals. Slack Alert Channels — Alert Types You choose which alerts are active for each client. Configure based on what matters for each client's current situation. Critical Alerts Hourly + → Zero-spend — active campaign with $0 in 24hrs → Sudden spend spike — campaign spend >2x 7-day trailing average → Ad rejected or disapproved → Account at risk or restricted by Meta Performance Alerts Daily + → Account ROAS drop >20% week-over-week → CPA breach >130% of target → Campaign ROAS below client-defined floor → Creative fatigue — frequency >3.5 with declining CTR → Underspending campaign — <50% of daily budget for 2+ consecutive days → Landing page CVR drop >25% week-over-week with stable traffic Creative Signals Daily / Weekly + → Breakthrough ad — ROAS >150% of account average at spend threshold → False breakthrough — strong day 1–2, drops below floor by day 5 → Thumbstop winner — hook rate >150% of account avg in first 24hrs → Hook rate decay — 3s view rate drops >25% from baseline → Weekly creative leaderboard — top 10 ads by spend, ROAS, CTR Competitive Intelligence Weekly + → Competitor new ad surge — competitor launches >5 ads in 7 days → New creative angles from top advertisers in category → Competitor offer or pricing change on key SKU Agents — Live & In Progress Creative Scoring Agent Live Query Meta data by client to rank ads by spend, ROAS, CPA, breakthrough days, and consistency score. Ask it anything — responds with charts, drill-downs, and follow-up analysis. Competitor Ad Detection Live Monitors your client's competitor watchlist daily. New ads from the last 24hrs surface in Slack with hook, landing page, and offer details. Daily Pulse Report Live Per-client Slack gets a daily snapshot: spend, revenue, ROAS, CPA vs. yesterday and 7-day average. No manual pulling. Ad Library Analyzer In Progress Analyzes hooks, scripts, and angles from category ads. Surfaces patterns and early signals. Configurable by brand watchlist, delivered to Slack on a schedule. What's coming. Things actively in motion that will affect how you work. CRO Department Hiring underway for a dedicated CRO role. → CRO covers conversion optimization — landing pages, offer structure, funnel testing → When it's live, you brief the CRO team the same way you brief the Creative Team: here's the problem, here's the data, here's what I need → Expands what you can deliver for clients without adding to your execution load Growth Strategist Transition → Now: If you share a client with a Growth Strategist, nothing changes. Collaborate as you normally do. → As the transition progresses: You absorb the client-facing and strategic responsibilities. Kevin and the AI systems are your support layer. → New clients going forward: You're the primary owner from day one. pages.text: Nurse Babes Brand Intelligence Briefing 7 of 7 steps complete • Generated May 14, 2026 • Strategist: Adrienne Ad Pros Brand Intelligence Prep 1. Brand Profile 2. Market Research 3. Competitor Intel 4. Assessment 5. Decisions 6. Creative Strategy 7. Creative Briefs Export All PDF Export This Step Brand Snapshot Brand Nurse Babes nursebabes.com Strategist Adrienne (Creative Director, Ad Pros) Session Start May 14, 2026 — same day AdPros onboarded + Comfort Club launched Customer Base 565,000+ Customers cited in brand story NPS 28.77 52% Promoters (per ICP survey) Tools Connected Tool Status Use Supabase Connected Brand record, metadata, VOC, insights Apify Connected Web scraping (Steps 2-3) Slack Connected Team share gates Google Drive Connected 16 source files ingested FireCrawl Not configured Apify handling scraping Sources Ingested (16) Category Sources Strategic Docs NB ICP from Survey, Brand Building & Mission (NB Identity 2026), Raw Research, Ronaldo's Holy Research Doc Quantitative Customer Survey (652 responses), KPI Dashboard (Jan 2025 – May 2026 MTD), Brand Content Calendar Competitive Competitor Master List (90+ brands), KURU 2024 Foot Pain Trends Whitepaper, Trustpilot Reviews, Social Media Comments Sheet Creative Top Ads Folder, Top UGC Videos, Top Statics, Top Kalodata (TikTok), Photoshoots (Nick Theriot), Creator Photos, Logos (NEW/OLD), Apparel Photos External Notion: Funnels Per Concept May 2026 Targets & Growth Levers AOV Target $110 Actual MTD: $117.90 (107%) Ad Spend $431k MTD: $154k (36%) CPA Max $60 Actual: $65.48 (+$5.48) Returning 684 MTD: 335 (49%) Growth Levers (Priority Order) LTV / Repeat purchase rate — #1 priority — currently ~10%, target lift toward 14%+ CAC — needs improvement, currently 9% over target Ad spend efficiency — scale to $431k while controlling CAC AOV — already stabilized at $117.90 vs $110 target Strategic Tensions Flagged for Step 5 1. Product brand vs. Identity brand. Mission docs have two competing positions: "we sell nurse shoes" vs. "Alo for nurses, help nurses show up strong." Both are alive in brand language. Spring 2025 logo refresh + apparel folder suggest identity-brand pivot is already in motion. 2. BOGO replacement vs. refinement. Buy 2 Get 1 Free has run since Aug 2024 (~21 months) and carries +27% AOV lift. Fatigued but functional. Kill it, refine it Hike-style, or layer non-BOGO acquisition alongside. 3. Knockoff defense. Active threats: nursebabesshop.com, comfortfitortho.com, 20+ Amazon listings, 2+ Walmart generics. Acknowledge in messaging or stay silent? Negative Persona (Locked) Nurse Babes is NOT for: People who want cheap shoes and don't care about support or how their feet feel after a long day People looking for stiff, bulky, medical-looking orthopedic shoes (no "doctor shoes" aesthetic) Anyone expecting shoes to instantly fix a serious medical issue without support, time, and care People who hate a roomier toe-box feel or only want narrow/tight-fitting shoes Customers who barely stand, walk, or deal with foot fatigue (won't feel full value) People who care only about style and not comfort, stability, slip resistance, or all-day wearability Anyone seeking specialty performance shoes for elite running, hiking, or sport-specific training Executive Summary Nurse Babes is a mature DTC footwear brand for nurses and healthcare professionals with 565,000+ customers , an established $117 AOV , and an NPS of 28.77 . The brand is in mid-transition: founded as a product brand ("affordable orthopedic-grade comfort for nurses") and now quietly evolving toward an identity brand ("Alo for nurses — help nurses show up strong"). Visible signals of the pivot include a spring 2025 logo refresh, an apparel content track, and explicit brand-doc language declaring "we don't sell shoes, we sell a way of being." The hero product is the Ortho Pro 1.0 , a lightweight slip-resistant supportive sneaker positioned in the affordable-comfort gap between $50 disposables and $150–$200 premium tier (Hoka, Clove, Brooks). The dominant offer is Buy 2 Get 1 Free , which has driven a +27% AOV lift over 17 months but is showing fatigue alongside a 2.24→1.93 Facebook ROAS decline as spend scales. Today (May 14, 2026) the brand launched Comfort Club , a loyalty/membership program with zero existing creative — the direct lever for the brand's #1 KPI priority of lifting repeat-purchase rate from ~10%. Brand DNA Positioning More of this: "We help nurses show up strong in hard lives." Identity-brand framing. Caregiver + Rebel archetype. Affordable comfort as a moral position ("comfort shouldn't be a luxury"). Built BY understanding nurses, FOR nurses. Peer-to-peer trust. Less of this: "We sell nurse shoes." Pure product-spec framing. Medical/clinical authority lane (that's Kuru's). "Doctor shoes" aesthetic. Premium-pricing posturing. Needs refinement Two competing positions still active in brand docs. Lock in Step 5. Tone of Voice Warm, peer-to-peer (nurse-to-nurse), no-BS, empathetic, confidence-building, affordable-but-not-cheap. Direct address ("you," "we"). Emotional but not melodramatic. Acknowledges sacrifice and pain without pity. Slogans in rotation: "Wear what feels good" / "Wear the feeling" / "Feel good. Look good. Show up strong." / "Because nurses deserve better." Confirmed from Brand Identity doc Brand Vocabulary Words We Use Cloud / walking on a cloud Support / supportive / supported All-day comfort Show up / show up strong Nurse, healthcare professional, RN Shift, 12-hour, on your feet Pain-free, relief Deserve, earned, sacrifice Sister, community, tribe Words We Don't Use Orthopedic (the LOOK, not the feeling) Sneaker / kicks (too casual) Cheap / discount (we're affordable, not cheap) Doctor shoe / clinical / medical-grade Athletic / performance / training Therapeutic (too clinical) Generic "shoe" speak Needs refinement Strategist confirmation required on exact list Brand Associations Associate With Nurses + healthcare worker culture Scrubs (Figs, Jaanuu adjacency) Cloud imagery + lightness Long shifts / hospital corridors Peer recommendation, nurse-to-nurse trust Identity wellness brands (Alo) "I should've done this sooner" regret Don't Associate With Athletic performance brands (Nike, ASICS) Medical device / orthotic shops Discount fashion (Payless, generic Amazon) "Mom shoes" / frumpy / Boomer Specialty hiking, running, court sports Founder Story The brand is named after the founder's vision: a shoe BY nurses FOR nurses, affordable, built for the realities of 12-hour shifts. The full founder narrative on nursebabes.com/pages/our-story is being updated — per Brand Identity doc, the brand is "working on getting a female to become face of the brand (coming soon)." Gap flagged: No founder-on-camera content folder, no CEO-led UGC, no founder origin video. Brand name implies founder is the face but the asset library has no founder-led content. Creative miss given the regret-reflex hook patterns customers convert on. Art Direction Logo system: Spring 2025 refresh produced a NEW wordmark with a THICK heavyweight variant. Old logos preserved. Suggests chunkier, more confident identity-brand direction. Photography: Single house photographer (Nick Theriot). April 2026 Ortho Collection shoot most recent. Style currently leans product-led + studio (per "01_propped" folder structure). Identity-brand pivot will need editorial/in-environment work. Apparel imagery: Dedicated content track in development. Creator pipeline: Managed in-house via influencer@nursebabes.com. Monthly cadence. Needs refinement Brand book / photography direction PDF not located in shared sources. Hero Customer (preliminary, deepened in Step 6) "Brenda" — the 52-year-old Registered Nurse Demographics: Female healthcare professional, 45–60+ (61% of base is 45+, 33% is 55+). 25+ years experience common. Work life: 72% on feet 8+ hours/day, 46% work shifts of 10+ hours. Primary pain: 55% cite foot pain as #1 challenge. 64% have back pain. 50% knee ...
