pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Nurse Babes Creator Content & Services Agreement Template v1 · May 26, 2026 · Reusable for Tier 1-4 creator deals Standard Agreement Template Legal review required. This template is a starting point informed by industry-standard creator agreements and the strategic decisions in the Nurse Babes Creator Plan v1. It is not a substitute for legal counsel. Have qualified attorney review before signing any creator. Fill in [bracketed placeholders] for each specific deal. Tier-specific values are noted in margin annotations. How to use this template Copy the template to a new document for each creator deal. Fill in all [placeholders] based on the agreed term sheet. Tier-specific values are listed in the annotations under each clause. Select the right tier and delete the others. Have legal review before sending to creator. Use DocuSign / HelloSign for execution. Store signed copies in [contract storage location] — never let originals live only in email. § Preamble This Creator Content & Services Agreement (this "Agreement" ) is entered into as of [EFFECTIVE DATE] (the "Effective Date" ) by and between: Nurse Babes , a [STATE] [ENTITY TYPE] with offices at [ADDRESS] (" Brand "); and [CREATOR LEGAL NAME] , an individual residing at [CREATOR ADDRESS] , professionally known as [CREATOR HANDLE / STAGE NAME] (" Creator "). Brand and Creator are each a " Party " and together the " Parties ." This Agreement sets forth the terms under which Creator will produce content and provide services for Brand. 1. Definitions "Content" means all photographs, videos, audio recordings, raw footage, b-roll, scripts, captions, edits, and other creative materials produced by Creator under this Agreement, whether delivered to Brand or retained by Creator. "Deliverables" means the specific Content items Creator is required to produce per Section 3, including all finished video pieces, hook variants, and supporting raw footage. "Paid Media" means any advertising placement that involves payment to a platform or distribution channel, including (without limitation) Meta Ads (Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network, Messenger, Threads), TikTok Ads, Google Ads, YouTube Ads, programmatic display, and email/SMS marketing. "Whitelisting" means Brand's authorization to run Paid Media advertising through Creator's social media handle(s), including via Meta Partnership Ads, TikTok Spark Ads, and equivalent platform mechanisms. "Attributed Sales" means sales of Brand's products tracked through Trybe, Social Snowball, or successor platforms as being driven by Creator's Content or Creator's personal affiliate code. "Tier" means the creator classification assigned to Creator: Tier 1 Proven , Tier 2 Active , Tier 3 Test , or Tier 4 Ambassador , per the Nurse Babes Creator Plan v1. "Term" has the meaning set forth in Section 9. 2. Tier Classification & Compensation 2.1 Tier Assignment Creator is engaged at [TIER 1 PROVEN / TIER 2 ACTIVE / TIER 3 TEST / TIER 4 AMBASSADOR] level. Compensation in this Section reflects the assigned Tier. Brand may promote or demote Creator's Tier at the end of any contract period based on performance, with corresponding compensation adjustments. 2.2 Base Compensation Brand shall pay Creator a base retainer of [$300 / $500 / N/A] per calendar month during the Term, payable on or before the first business day of each month. Tier Base Retainer Tier 1 Proven (SKU B) $500/month Tier 2 Active (SKU A) $300/month Tier 3 Test (SKU T) $0 base (product sample only) Tier 4 Ambassador (SKU AMB) $0 base + 15% affiliate commission only 2.3 Performance Revenue Share For Tier 1 creators only, Brand shall pay Creator [10% / 12% (Premium)] of Attributed Sales tracked through Trybe-attribution for each Deliverable, for a period of twelve (12) months from each Deliverable's first launch date. Tier 2 and 3 creators are not eligible for revenue share. Tier 4 ambassadors are compensated solely through the Affiliate Commission in Section 2.5. 2.4 Winner Bonus For Tier 1 creators, Brand shall pay Creator a one-time bonus of $500 per Deliverable that achieves "Winner" status, defined as: (a) cumulative Brand ad spend on that Deliverable exceeding $10,000, AND (b) return on ad spend equal to or greater than Brand's account-level ROAS for the trailing 30-day period. Winner Bonus is paid within 30 days of confirmation. 2.5 Affiliate Commission Creator will receive a personal affiliate code via Social Snowball. Brand shall pay Creator a commission of [10% (Tier 1-3) / 15% (Tier 4 Ambassador)] on all Attributed Sales tracked through Creator's affiliate code, paid monthly via Social Snowball within the standard payout window. 2.6 Product Allocation Brand shall provide Creator with sample product as required for content production, up to a maximum of [2 pairs per quarter] for Tier 1-2 creators. Tier 3 Test creators receive one (1) sample pair at engagement and become eligible for additional product upon advancement to Tier 2. 2.7 Payment Method & Currency All payments shall be made in U.S. Dollars via Trybe (for base + revenue share + winner bonus) and Social Snowball (for affiliate commission). Payments held by either platform are subject to platform terms and processing windows. 3. Scope of Work & Deliverables 3.1 Monthly Deliverables (Tier 1 SKU B) Ten (10) full video Deliverables per calendar month, each between 15 and 60 seconds in length, formatted 9:16 vertical for use across Meta Reels, TikTok, Instagram Stories, and equivalent placements. Two (2) fresh hook variants per calendar month, each approximately 5 seconds in length, designed for A/B testing against existing top-performing creative. Raw footage and b-roll from each shoot, delivered alongside finished pieces. 3.1.alt Monthly Deliverables (Tier 2 SKU A) Fifteen (15) full video Deliverables per calendar month, same specifications as 3.1. 3.1.alt Monthly Deliverables (Tier 3 SKU T) One (1) to two (2) Deliverables over the 30-day initial engagement period. Advancement to Tier 2 is contingent on Brand approval of submitted Deliverables meeting brand voice and quality standards. 3.2 Content Briefs Brand shall deliver written content briefs to Creator via Trybe at least seven (7) days before each Deliverable due date. Briefs will specify: subject, intended hook, key messaging points, format, and any required visual or copy elements. Creator agrees to follow brief guidance unless Brand expressly grants creative latitude. 3.3 Submission & Approval Timeline Stage SLA Creator submits first cut after brief delivery Within 7 calendar days Brand provides approval, revision request, or rejection Within 48 hours of submission Creator submits revised cut (if requested) Within 5 calendar days of revision request Final delivery in usable format (MP4, 1080p+, source audio) Within 48 hours of approval 3.4 Quality Standards Resolution: minimum 1080p (Full HD) for all video Deliverables Audio: clean and intelligible voice recording where script is present Format: MP4 or MOV, H.264 codec, native vertical 9:16 aspect ratio (1080×1920) FTC #ad / #sponsored disclosure visible within first 3 seconds of every paid Deliverable Brand product (Ortho Pro 1.0 or current featured SKU) clearly visible in finished piece 3.5 Compliance Standards All Content produced under this Agreement must comply with the Nurse Babes Brand Voice Guardrails (Schedule A). Failure to meet compliance standards is grounds for rejection of submission, revision without compensation, and counts toward Creator's strike record. 4. Grant of Rights This is the most important section of this Agreement. Brand requires perpetual paid-media rights on all Content delivered under this Agreement. This is non-negotiable. Brand has previously lost significant revenue due to expiring usage rights and will not enter into agreements that restrict long-term use of Content. 4.1 Perpetual Paid-Media Usage Rights Creator grants Brand a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to use, ...

pages.title: Nurse Babes Creator Plan v1
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Nurse Babes Creator Plan v1 Strategist: Adrienne · Drafted May 21, 2026 · 90-day execution window Ad Pros Creator Operations Executive Summary Nurse Babes is targeting $1M/month in Meta spend , with 50% ($500k) driven by creator content . To get there, the brand needs 25 meaningful active creators producing on a steady cadence and 10-20 new creators tested every month to keep the funnel alive. That ambition exists today — but the operating scaffold doesn't. Two creator platforms (Trybe + Social Snowball) run in parallel with no defined ownership, retainer offers vary case-by-case, and there's no published KPI framework. This plan fixes that. This is the v1 operating blueprint. It maps two-platform roles, retainer SKU standardization, KPIs, dashboards, operating cadence, and a 90-day rollout. It also ties the creator pipeline directly to the Comfort Club ambassador layer — the long-term flywheel. How this plan works — division of labor. Ad Pros provides the structure : strategy, frameworks, briefs, performance analysis, and creator-tier definitions. The Nurse Babes team executes : daily submission review, compliance checks, brief distribution to creators on Trybe / Discord / Snowball, Tier 3 creator outreach + onboarding, and day-to-day creator relationship management. 1. North Star & Goals North Star $500k/mo Creator-driven Meta spend (50% of $1M scale target) Active Roster 25 Meaningful, performing creators Test Velocity 10-20 New creators tested per month Window 90 days May 21 - Aug 21, 2026 Strategic Goals Replace the stale-hook portfolio — feed Ad Pros' 25-30 NEW concepts/month testing volume with creator-led UGC. Lower CAC to $60 max ($55 preferred) — creator content historically outperforms templated brand ads on this metric in DTC. Build the long-term ambassador flywheel — Comfort Club Month 6 milestone unlocks creator opportunity; convert subscribers into UGC producers. Diversify channel risk — same creator content powers Meta (paid), TikTok Shop (organic + creator-driven), Google Discovery, and email/SMS retention. Lock perpetual usage rights — no more "At Home Dog Review" losses ($1M revenue ad killed by expired rights). 2. KPI Framework Lagging KPIs (outcomes) KPI Target Reporting Cadence Owner Creator-driven monthly spend $500k/mo at scale Monthly Ad Pros media buyer Creator-content CPA ≤ blended account CPA ($60 max) Bi-weekly Ad Pros media buyer Creator-content ROAS ≥ account ROAS (2.0+) Bi-weekly Ad Pros media buyer Active creators producing this month 25 by Day 90 Weekly Client's team (reported into weekly brief) New creators tested this month 10-20 Weekly Client's team (reported into weekly brief) Top-creator retention (%) ≥ 80% retain month-over-month Monthly Client's team (reported in monthly roster scorecard) Comfort Club ambassador conversion 5+ subscribers/quarter promoted to ambassador (M6+) Quarterly Ad Pros + client Leading Indicators (the dials we manage daily/weekly) Indicator Healthy Range Why it matters Creators in pipeline (applications + outreach) 30-50 active conversations Pipeline-to-active conversion runs ~30%. To land 10-20 new tests/month we need 30-50 in pipe. Briefs delivered to creators per week 15-25 Brief throughput is the bottleneck. 2 standard SKUs (15 video or 10 video + 2 hooks) keeps it scalable. Submission turnaround time ≤ 7 days from brief to first cut Slow submissions = stale content. 7-day SLA enforced. Approval-to-launch time ≤ 48 hours from submission to live ad Whitelist + Spark Ads infrastructure enables fast deployment. % of submissions meeting brand voice + compliance ≥ 80% Below 80% signals brief quality issues. Above 95% means we're not pushing creative variance enough. Top 3 creators' weekly output 4-6 deliverables each Top performers drive disproportionate share. Their cadence is the leading indicator of creator-spend ceiling. Success Criteria by Milestone Milestone Target State Day 30 Access secured (Discord, Social Snowball admin, Trybe). Roster audited. 5 creators producing under new standardized briefs. First AdPros-built campaign live. Day 60 10-12 active creators. First whitelist scaled to $50k+ spend. Bi-weekly cadence operational. Compliance review baked in. Day 90 25 active creators. Creator-content driving $200k+/mo spend (40% of $500k target trajectory). Ambassador funnel design locked for Q4 launch. Month 6 $500k/mo creator spend hit. Comfort Club Month-6 milestone activates first cohort of subscriber-ambassadors. Revenue-share pilot launches with top 3 ambassadors. 3. Two-Platform Operating Model The fix: Trybe and Social Snowball are not competitors — they own different jobs. Stop running them in parallel with no division of labor. Lock the roles below. Trybe → Paid-Performance UGC Owns: Production of creator-led UGC content explicitly intended to power paid ad accounts. Mechanic: 10% of creator earnings on flat-fee / retainer, OR 1.5% of Trybe-attributed sales. Integration: Direct Shopify sync + Meta Partnership Ads launch from approved submissions in one click. Best for: Feeding the 25-30 NEW concepts/month testing volume. Whitelisted Meta ads at scale. Decision rule: If the content is going to be a Meta ad, route through Trybe. Social Snowball → Affiliate, Referral, Ambassador Owns: Customer-to-affiliate conversion, TikTok Shop creator tracking, Comfort Club ambassador layer. Mechanic: $199/mo + 3% of affiliate-generated revenue. Integration: Shopify-native, TikTok Shop tracking, UGC media library that auto-saves affiliate-tagged posts. Best for: The "every-customer-is-a-potential-affiliate" model post-purchase. Comfort Club Month-6 ambassador unlock. Decision rule: If the content is going to drive organic reach + attribution-trackable referrals, route through Social Snowball. Decision Tree: Which platform owns this creator? Creator type Platform Why New tester / brief-fulfillment / paid-content focus Trybe Optimized for content production + Meta ad launch Proven creator on retainer + revenue share Trybe (primary) + Social Snowball (referral layer) Trybe handles production; Social Snowball captures organic-conversion referrals Customer-turned-affiliate (post-purchase) Social Snowball Auto-convert checkout into affiliate Comfort Club Member at Month 6 milestone (Ambassador unlock) Social Snowball (affiliate) + Trybe (if producing content) Affiliate-track via Snowball, content-produce via Trybe TikTok Shop creator Social Snowball Native TT Shop integration + UGC library 4. Creator Tiering & Standardized Retainer SKUs Tier Profile SKU Compensation Volume Goal Tier 1: Proven 3+ months producing, content scaled to paid, retention proof SKU B: 10 videos / 2 hooks per month $500/mo + 10% revenue share + perpetual usage rights 5-8 creators by Day 90 Tier 2: Active 1-3 months producing, meeting brand voice, in performance optimization SKU A: 15 videos per month $300/mo + standard usage rights, no revenue share yet 12-17 creators by Day 90 Tier 3: Test New, first submission window, gifting + brief delivery SKU T: Sample pair + brief, 1-2 submissions over 30 days Product only ($20/pair COGS estimate). Move to Tier 2 if 1+ submission meets bar. 10-20 new tests/month Tier 4: Ambassador Comfort Club Month-6 unlock (subscribers who completed the milestone progression) SKU AMB: Affiliate code + 15% revenue share on referrals 15% commission via Social Snowball + content opportunity via Trybe if interested 5+ activated by Day 90 + Quarter 4 cohort scale-up Drop case-by-case retainer math. Every creator slots into one of these four SKUs. If a creator request doesn't fit, the answer is "Tier 2 SKU A at $300/mo" until they prove they're Tier 1. This kills the chaos. 5. Operating Cadence Cadence Action Owner Output Daily Submission review — new creator deliverables approved / declined / revision-requested Client's team Status updated in Trybe; flagged items shared with Ad Pros Daily Compliance check on submissions (no health claims, brand voice, asset quality) Client's team (using Ad Pros ...

pages.title: Nurse Babes × Jen the Piercer
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Nurse Babes × Jen the Piercer Deal Proposal & Term Sheet · Drafted May 26, 2026 · Strategist: Adrienne Dyer Tier 1 Proven · Cross-Over Loyalist Variant Why We Want To Work With You Jen, we've spent the last quarter doing a deep dive on what's actually working for Nurse Babes. The data showed us something we didn't expect: about 13% of our customer base isn't nurses at all . They're hairdressers, teachers, baristas, piercers, retail floor managers — anyone who spends their whole day on their feet doing real work. You showed up as one of the most compelling representatives of that customer. Your content didn't just convert; it cracked open a segment we hadn't been able to reach with nurse-led ads. That made you strategically important — not just another creator, but the anchor for an expanded customer base. This proposal is built around making sure we both win from that. The Deal At A Glance Base Retainer $500/mo Tier 1 Proven SKU Revenue Share 10% on attributed sales · 12 mo per piece Content Delivery 10 + 2 10 videos + 2 hooks per month 1. Compensation Stack Component Amount Notes Monthly base retainer $500 Paid first of every month via Trybe Performance bonus — paid-media 10% of Trybe-attributed sales Tracked per content piece for 12 months from launch Affiliate commission — organic / TT Shop 10% of Social Snowball-attributed sales Personal affiliate code, paid monthly Winner bonus $500 per piece Unlocked when a content piece scales to $10k+ ad spend at or above account ROAS Product Unlimited samples Up to 2 pairs per quarter for new colorways / launches Upside math: If one of your pieces becomes a Top Performer (we use 4-5 per quarter to drive ~$50k+/mo in spend), the 10% revenue share alone can be worth $5k-$15k/month on its own — on top of base + affiliate. 2. Content Scope Monthly deliverables 10 full video deliverables — 9:16 vertical (Meta Reels / TikTok / IG Stories), 15-60 seconds each 2 fresh hook variants per month — ~5-second openers we can A/B test against existing winners Mix of acquisition (TOF), consideration (MOF), and retention angles — we'll send specific briefs each cycle Brief assignments (initial 3-month rotation) Brief Angle Cross-Over Loyalist "I'm a piercer, not a nurse. These got me through 9 hours behind the chair." Regret Reflex "I waited too long to try these. Don't make the same mistake." The Setting Twist Filmed at the piercing studio — mid-day, between clients, real working context Hour-by-Hour "Hour 1. Hour 5. Hour 9. The shoes don't quit. Neither do you." At-Home Lifestyle Casual review setting — couch, kitchen, post-shift unwind. (If you have a pet, even better) Comparison "I used to wear [X]. Then I tried these. Here's what changed." Service-level expectations 7-day turnaround from brief delivery to first cut 48-hour turnaround on approved revisions Submissions delivered via Trybe Bi-weekly check-in with Ad Pros creator lead 3. Usage Rights The most important part of this deal. We lost a $1M-revenue creator ad last year because the usage rights expired. We're not letting that happen again. Our standard is perpetual rights — we'll never revoke, you'll never have to renew, and we both get the upside of content compounding over time. What you grant Nurse Babes Perpetual, worldwide paid-media usage rights on all delivered content + raw / unselected footage Meta Partnership Ads whitelist authorization — we run ads through your handle TikTok Spark Ads authorization — same on TikTok Edit / derivative rights — we can recut, repurpose, and remix delivered footage into new ads without re-shooting Name + likeness usage in paid creative for the term + perpetual on any signed assets What we don't take You retain ownership of your content for your own organic channels You can use the work in your portfolio, reels, and personal marketing We don't restrict your other paid partnerships outside of direct competitors (see Exclusivity below) 4. Exclusivity & Protections Category exclusivity No direct nurse-footwear / healthcare-comfort competitor work during the term + 30 days post (Clove, Kuru, Snibbs, Nurse Mates, Crocs Bistro, Comfortorthowear, Hike Footwear) First-look right We get 7 days to match any competing nurse-footwear approach for 12 months after term end Adjacent categories Wide open. Apparel, scrubs, wellness, fitness, accessories — all fine. We won't restrict your business. FTC disclosure #ad or #sponsored required on all paid placements, visible in first 3 seconds 5. Term & Renewal Initial term 3 months (locked). This gives both sides enough cycles to know if the fit works. Auto-renewal triggers Contract auto-renews for additional 3-month periods if trailing 30-day metrics meet: CPA on your content ≤ blended account CPA ROAS on your content ≥ 2.0 Submission cadence met (≥ 80% on-time deliveries) Tier promotion path If your content drives $50k+/month in attributed Meta spend at or above target metrics for 2 consecutive months , you unlock SKU B Premium : $750/month base + 12% revenue share + priority brief assignment. Termination Either side can terminate with 30 days' written notice. Content already delivered remains covered by perpetual usage rights. 6. Ambassador Track (Optional, Open Now) Beyond paid content production, we're building an Ambassador layer that scales creator economics significantly. Ambassadors get: 15% revenue share on all customer referrals (vs the 10% on attributed content) Early access to new product launches before public Co-branded creator drops (limited editions named after / styled with you) Equity-style milestones — quarterly bonuses tied to total contribution to the brand You'd be one of the first 5 external ambassadors in the program. We'd love to discuss whether that fits where you want this relationship to go. 7. Communication & Tools Brief delivery Trybe platform (with email backup) Content submission Trybe Affiliate tracking Social Snowball (you'll get a unique code + dashboard) Day-to-day comms Dedicated Slack channel or Discord (you pick) Performance updates Bi-weekly: what scaled, what we're testing next Payments Monthly via Trybe (US bank transfer or Stripe) 8. Brand Voice Guardrails One thing we ask: certain language carries legal risk for the brand in paid advertising. Customer reviews are exempt — you can quote a customer saying anything — but content written or spoken in your voice can't make health/medical claims. Phrases to avoid in your voice "Pain-free" or "eliminates pain" "Treats / cures / heals / fixes" — anything implying medical treatment "Medical-grade" / "clinically proven" / "FDA approved" "Plantar fasciitis cure" or similar condition-specific claims "Doctor / podiatrist recommended" unless we have a specific named doctor on file What you can absolutely say "All-day comfort" "Built for long days on your feet" "Supportive" / "easy on your feet" "Show up strong" Your personal experience — how they feel, what they replaced, why you wear them What Happens Next You read this and tell us what's not working for you. Real conversation, no boilerplate. We want to make this a deal both sides are excited about. We finalize the term sheet — this doc with any edits we agree on. Contract paperwork — our legal template signed within 7 days. Standard creator agreement with the perpetual rights language we discussed. Onboarding — Trybe + Social Snowball setup, Discord/Slack access, first brief delivery. Month 1 starts — first 10 videos + 2 hooks, with regular bi-weekly check-ins. Why This Deal Structure We've thought hard about how to structure creator partnerships that actually work long-term. The pattern we keep seeing across brands: one-off deals leave money on the table for both sides. Creators have to keep hunting for the next brand, brands have to keep recruiting and onboarding from scratch. This deal is built on the opposite principle — we lock in a working relationship for a long-term arc, with performance triggers that compound as your content compounds. If our content ...

pages.title: Nurse Babes — Meta Attribution Benchmarks
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Nurse Babes — Meta Attribution Benchmarks Multiple lenses (incl. 4 in-platform attribution settings) · trailing 90 days · target: $60 business-wide ncCPA Attribution Analysis Meta benchmarks to hit a $60 new-customer CPA A read of the trailing 90 days across in-platform Meta, TripleWhale Last Click, and TripleWhale First Click — with the targets needed to bring business-wide ncCPA back to $60. Feb 13 – May 13, 2026 Period Trailing 90 days $1.1M Total spend All paid channels 17,010 New customers Need 18,419 to hit target $64.97 Current ncCPA vs $60.00 target The headline Meta benchmarks — multiple lenses To return business-wide ncCPA to $60 at current spend levels, here’s what Meta needs to deliver under different attribution lenses, derived from the trailing 90 days ($1.1M Meta spend). The two TripleWhale cards below are cross-channel views counting new customers only. The in-platform Meta panel underneath shows the same math translated across four Meta Ads Manager attribution settings. TripleWhale — Last Click Meta Benchmark 17% gap Inside TripleWhale, this gives 100% of the credit for a new customer to whichever channel they LAST clicked before buying. It’s a cross-channel view — different from Meta’s own in-platform attribution, which counts purchases within Meta’s own attribution window regardless of what other channels were clicked afterwards. Current CPA $163.90 → Benchmark CPA $139.51 Distance to benchmark 85% of the way there Gap to close: $24.39 (17.5% above target) Organic Lift 52.0% Meta share of paid NCs 73.9% TripleWhale — First Click Meta Benchmark 36% gap Gives 100% of the credit to whichever channel FIRST introduced a customer to Nurse Babes — even if they came back through different channels later. Answers: where are new customers actually discovering the brand for the first time? Current CPA $329.17 → Benchmark CPA $242.38 Distance to benchmark 74% of the way there Gap to close: $86.79 (35.8% above target) Organic Lift 76.8% Meta share of paid NCs 76.1% In-Platform Meta · Meta Ads Manager Meta Benchmarks across four attribution settings Regression-derived · daily 90-day data Meta Ads Manager shows different numbers depending on the attribution setting applied. All four below count both new and returning customer purchases — that’s unavoidable in-platform. Each benchmark is derived from a linear regression of that metric against business-wide ncCPA across 90 daily data points — the CPA / ROAS level at which business-wide ncCPA reaches $60. Pick the setting the team is operating against and hold to that benchmark consistently. Attribution Setting Current CPA Benchmark CPA Current ROAS Benchmark ROAS R² (CPA/ROAS) Blended (default) Includes view-through. Loosest view. $59.05 $53.61 1.88x 2.16x 0.77 / 0.47 7-Day Click All Conversions Click only, no view-through. Counts repeat purchases per customer. $66.52 $59.99 1.67x 1.84x 0.75 / 0.41 7-Day Click First Conversion Click only. Counts only first purchase per customer (closer to new-customer view). $67.78 $61.17 1.65x 1.86x 0.82 / 0.64 Incremental First Conversion Meta’s incrementality model. Strictest — only credits truly incremental conversions. $70.24 $63.77 1.60x 1.88x 0.81 / 0.66 How these benchmarks were built: linear regression of each Meta metric against daily business-wide ncCPA over 90 days. The benchmark is the metric value at which the regression predicts business-wide ncCPA = $60. The four metrics need different improvements (~9-10% CPA reduction, +12-15% ROAS lift) because each lens correlates with the business outcome a bit differently. 7-Day Click First Conversion CPA has the tightest fit (R² = 0.82) — most predictive single in-platform metric. Higher R² = more reliable signal. Why the First Click number looks so much higher Only about 1 in 4 new customers (23%) first discovered Nurse Babes through a paid ad. The other 77% first heard about the brand somewhere else — a friend, an email, an organic search, direct traffic — and only came back through Meta later to actually buy. So when First Click attribution asks “who introduced this customer?” — Meta gets credit for fewer of those first hellos. That’s why the same Meta spend looks roughly 2× more expensive under First Click vs Last Click. It’s not that Meta suddenly became inefficient — it’s that First Click is measuring something different. The structural shift What changed since we last hit target Feb 2026 was the most recent month with business-wide ncCPA at or below $60 (actual $57.70). Since then, paid scaled faster than new-customer volume — and organic didn’t scale alongside it. Metric Feb 2026 Trailing 90d Δ Spend $260,582 $1,105,125 +324% Shopify new customers 4,516 17,010 +277% New customer revenue $464,098 $1,851,140 +299% Business-wide ncCPA $57.70 $64.97 +13% In-Platform Meta CPA $53.42 $66.52 +11% Spend per day +33% $9.3K/day → $12.3K/day In-Platform Meta CPA (7DC) +11% $53.42 → $66.52 Organic mix ~ Flat Did not scale with paid How to use these three numbers One is what we manage to. Two tell us what’s going on underneath. Each benchmark answers a different question. Used together, they give a clear picture of Meta’s real contribution to the business. The day-to-day number — In-Platform Meta ($59.99 CPA / 2.21x ROAS) This is the number the Growth Marketer watches every day inside Meta Ads Manager. If in-platform CPA drifts above $59.99 (or ROAS drops below 2.21x), that’s the first signal something inside the Meta account needs attention — creative, audience, bid strategy, or testing cadence. The closing-credit check — TW Last Click ($139.51 CPA) A weekly cross-channel view. Different from in-platform because it asks: when Meta gets credit head-to-head against every other channel, how much is it actually closing? If in-platform looks good but TW Last Click is rough, it means Meta is taking credit in-platform for purchases another channel actually closed. The discovery check — TW First Click ($242.38 CPA) A monthly check on whether Meta is actually bringing new people into the brand vs. mostly closing customers who already knew about Nurse Babes. If Meta hits in-platform and Last Click but First Click stays rough, that’s a conversation about top-of-funnel — not an automatic spend reallocation. These benchmarks are math, not a verdict. They tell us what Meta would need to deliver under each lens to hit $60 — they don’t account for halo effects between channels, brand-search lift, or the work Meta does that other tools end up taking credit for. We use them as guardrails, not as a single source of truth. ✓ Re-benchmark monthly · adjust if spend scale or organic mix shifts materially

pages.title: Performance Partner Positioning
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Performance Partner Positioning Identity-led positioning for Ad Pros and the operators we serve Executive Summary Performance partner for 8-figure operators . Six words. Two identity claims. Zero filler. The category Ad Pros owns and the audience we exist to serve, said in a single line that filters the right brands in and the wrong ones out — before the discovery call ever starts. Hero / IG bio / deck cover · Performance partner for 8-figure operators 01 The thesis Identity is faster than belief. Beliefs require evidence, argument, and overcoming the backfire effect. Identity just requires offering a label that flatters who someone already wants to be. Once a person accepts a label, their beliefs and behaviors reorganize to defend the self-concept — they argue themselves into consistency. For positioning, this means leading with who someone is, not what they should think. "Performance partner for 8-figure operators" reads like a category, not a tagline. It sounds like a thing that exists — a recognizable role in the market — not a slogan a company invented for itself. Why this line works 02 The two identities Partner and operator. Peer to peer. Vendors serve founders. Agencies pitch brands. Partners and operators sit at the same table. The grammar of the relationship matches the economics of the model — a kicker on CPA, fees on the line, equity-like exposure across the Creator Performance Network. A Agency identity Performance partner Ad Pros is the only agency that puts its fee on the line next to the client's CPA. The pricing model, the kicker structure, and the Creator Network 7/3 split all express the same idea: shared outcomes, not billable hours. Recruits senior buyers and strategists. Repels agency-hopping account managers. B Client identity 8-figure operator A founder or CEO who treats ad spend as a P&L line, not a marketing expense. They allocate capital and expect return. They self-select into the relationship — and self-select out of price-shopping it. Implicit qualifier: $300K+/month spend, $10M+ revenue. Aspirational for 7-figure brands. 03 The contrast that makes it bite Partner / vendor. Operator / founder. Identity claims do their best work in contrast. The asymmetry below is what every part of the Ad Pros model is already saying — the positioning line just makes it visible in nine words. PARTNER MODEL Performance partner Fee scales with the client's CPA performance Kicker on outcomes, retainer covers the floor Senior team treats the account like a P&L Creator Network: 7% kept, 3% to creators — equity-like exposure Sits at the table, not across it VENDOR MODEL Generic agency Flat retainer, indifferent to outcomes Hours billed regardless of result Account managers rotated, ownership diffuse Creators paid flat per-asset, no upside Reports up to procurement, not the founder 04 Why this line specifically Why "for" matters more than "the." 1 The audience is the subject of the promise "Performance partner for 8-figure operators" makes the operator the protagonist. " The performance partner" makes Ad Pros the protagonist. Audience-first lines win attention faster. 2 Six words, two identity claims, zero filler Every word is load-bearing. Drop any one and the meaning collapses. That's the test of a positioning line worth keeping. 3 It qualifies silently A $2M brand reading this knows it isn't for them. A $40M brand reading this feels seen. The line filters before the discovery call — no "who we work with" page required. 4 Partner + operator implies equality Partners and operators sit at the same table. The framing is peer-to-peer — exactly the energy needed walking into a pricing negotiation where the client is testing whether Ad Pros will fold. 5 It reads like a category, not a slogan "Performance partner for 8-figure operators" sounds like a job that exists in the market. That's rare. Most agency taglines sound invented; this one sounds discovered. 05 The market context Identity labels in the wild. "Operator" is the dominant identity label across the ecommerce ecosystem — Klaviyo, Shopify, Triple Whale, Northbeam all lean on it. "Founder" is more romantic but generic. "Merchant" is humble and craft-oriented. "Rebel" peaked in the 2015–2020 DTC wave and is fading. The lane Ad Pros can credibly claim — performance partner — is uncontested at the agency level. Operator Dominant. Klaviyo, Shopify, attribution tools. Implies P&L ownership, not just selling. Founder Universal but generic. Romantic, lower-bar — anyone who started a thing qualifies. Merchant Shopify's preferred internal label. Humble, craft-oriented, deliberately less "tech startup." Rebel / disruptor Peaked 2015–2020. Still potent for emerging-category brands; fading otherwise. 7/8/9-figure Revenue-tier identity. Self-selecting, status-conferring, used heavily by agencies and educators. Brand builder Faded post-2022 as the "build a real brand" narrative collided with CAC reality. The open lane Most agencies still pitch "founders" and "brands." Tools have already established "operator" credibility — Ad Pros can borrow that and narrow it: not just any operator, but the kind who runs ad spend like a CFO would. "Performance partner" is uncontested at the agency level. 06 Where to deploy Surfaces and grammar. The line works because it is declarative and isolated. Surrounded by other claims, it loses weight. Lead with the audience identity ("for 8-figure operators") and let "performance partner" explain why we exist. USE HERE Website hero — first three seconds Sales deck cover slide LinkedIn company tagline IG bios — Ad Pros and Nehal Pre-discovery one-pager Email signatures, client-facing team AVOID HERE Buried inside body paragraphs Mixed with other claims or slogans Beneath a longer "we do X, Y, Z" header Followed by "and we also help with…" Diluted with adjectives ("the leading…") Surrounded by competing positioning lines 07 Trade-offs to acknowledge What this line costs. "8-figure" is a hard gate. Aspirational sub-$10M brands will lean in; sub-$5M brands will self-select out. That's intentional given the $300K/month spend baseline in the pricing model — but it is a real trade. The line will cost mid-7-figure brands who would have paid. The argument for accepting that trade: tiers attract upward, services get shopped on price. "Performance partner" reads cleanly to sophisticated operators and slightly generic to newer founders. That trade — broad appeal for sharp targeting — is the right one for a brand built around CPA-linked pricing. The deliberate choice 08 Recommendation Lock the line. Roll it across surfaces. Adopt "Performance partner for 8-figure operators" as the primary positioning line. Test against three current clients and three target prospects before committing site-wide. Once validated, deploy across web hero, sales deck, social bios, and signatures within the same week — consistency is what makes a category claim feel real. 6 Words 2 Identity claims 1 Category owned

pages.title: Performance Pricing Model
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Performance Pricing Model Proposal 3 — Pay for results Pricing Proposal · v1 Hit $60 CPA , we win together. A flat $10,000 base retainer plus a variable media buying fee, both scaled by how well we hit the $60 CPA target. When we beat $60, we earn an additional spend bonus. When we miss, our fee shrinks to share the pain. Baseline Scenario $300,000/month spend at $60 CPA ~5,000 conversions/month at target efficiency. Total Fee $20,250 % of Spend 6.75% Better CPA → we earn more Lower CPA increases the fee multiplier and unlocks the spend bonus. CPA $50 ↗ Crushing it $10 below target. 1.17× multiplier + 0.42% spend bonus. Growth 5. Scale 6. Breakthrough Supporting Info Executive Summary Six service combos. One pricing model. Built to scale with spend. Ad Pros now operates against a unified pricing architecture: flat base retainers for fixed-deliverable services , tiered variable rates for spend-scaling services , and a performance-discount mechanic tied to new customer ROAS. This document maps six combo plans against a $1M / month managed-spend scenario. 6 Combo Plans $1M Spend Scenario 5 Discount Tiers Combo summary (no discount applied) Sorted by total monthly fee descending. Most prospects spending $250K–$750K/mo will land here at ~$69K/mo on $1M of spend (6.9% of spend). CPN is your second-largest revenue line on Scale and Breakthrough. 23.5% of Scale and 26.3% of Breakthrough comes from CPN. Whoever owns CPN owns major revenue. pages.title: Pulse Framework
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Pulse Framework Subscription Intelligence Layer · Internal v1.0 Vol. 01 · Internal · Nehal · Founder The Subscription Intelligence Layer A unified agent framework for delivering proactive, opinionated, daily intelligence to Ad Pros clients — built on one engine, three subscription tiers, eight digest types. 8 agents 3 tiers 6 weeks to launch ~95% gross margin 01 Executive Summary 02 Product Architecture 03 Data Schema 04 Agent Framework 05 Sample Digests 06 SOPs 07 Pricing & Rollout 08 Tech Stack 01.01 — The Thesis Most agencies hide behind monthly reports. The agency that shows up in a client's inbox every morning at 8am — with sharp, opinionated, data-backed intelligence — is perceived as 10x more valuable, regardless of actual hours worked. Core Insight We are not building seven agents. We are building one agent framework with seven subscription types. The product is the subscription model itself — a daily, chat-extensible intelligence layer that sits on top of our existing data infrastructure. 01.02 — The Pattern Every agent in the framework follows the same primitive: 01 SUBSCRIBE Client opts in to a digest type with optional filter (campaign, concept, URL, competitor) 02 DIGEST Agent runs daily at 8am client local — produces a structured 5-10 metric brief 03 DELIVER Email + Slack + in-app, with a one-click "chat for details" affordance 04 CHAT Client clicks → loads full context into AI chat → asks any follow-up question 01.03 — Why This Wins α Familiar UX Subscribe → daily digest → click for depth. Same pattern as Stripe email, GitHub digests, Bloomberg terminal alerts. Zero learning curve for clients. β One Engine All eight agents share the same backend: BigQuery + Meta API + competitive intelligence pipeline. Adding new agent types is hours, not weeks. γ Productized Moat The competitor digest is built on our 5K-ads/day pipeline. No one else in agency-land can ship this. It justifies premium retainers. 01.04 — The Numbers Agents 08 3 default · 5 add-on Tiers 03 Pulse · Watch · Intel Build Weeks 06 framework + 8 agents Revenue Lift 22% est. retainer uplift 01.05 — The Build Order Framework first. Subscription DB, scheduler, digest formatter, chat handoff. This is the keystone — everything else depends on it. Pulse tier (default for all clients). Daily KPI Brief, Weekly Goals vs Actual, Spend Pacing. Ship these as included value. Watch tier (per-client opt-in). Concept, Campaign, Landing Page monitors — one engine, three filter types. Top 5 Concept Spend is the differentiator. Intel tier (premium add-on). Competitor Daily — the moat. Powered by existing 5K-ads/day pipeline. 02.01 — Three Tiers · One Engine The architecture is intentionally simple: three subscription tiers stacked on a shared backend. Each tier represents a different perceived value level — and a different price point. PULSE Included Default for every client The baseline intelligence layer. Turned on day one of onboarding. No opt-in needed. Daily KPI Brief Weekly Goals vs Actual Spend Pacing Watchdog WATCH $X / mo / sub Subscribe to anything Per-client opt-in. Subscribe to monitor any campaign, concept, landing page, or top-spend cohort. Concept Monitor Campaign Monitor Landing Page Monitor Top 5 Concept Spend INTEL $XX / mo The moat Premium add-on, powered by our 5,000 ads/day competitive intelligence pipeline. Competitor Daily 02.02 — Shared Infrastructure All eight agents pull from the same five data sources, write to the same digest store, and deliver through the same channels. This is the leverage point — adding a ninth agent type costs days, not weeks. Sources BigQuery (perf data) Meta API (live) Google Ads API AdScan (competitors) Page Scraper (LPs) Engine Subscription DB · Scheduler · Digest Formatter (Claude) · Chat Handoff Agents Daily KPI Brief Weekly Goals Spend Pacing Concept Monitor Campaign Monitor LP Monitor Top 5 Concept Spend Competitor Daily Delivery Email (SendGrid) Slack DM In-app inbox Chat handoff (Claude) 03.01 — Data Schema Five tables. Postgres on Supabase. The schema is deliberately minimal — every agent type fits into the same five-table model via the filter_payload jsonb and agent_targets join. Why JSONB for Filters Each agent type has different config needs (a competitor agent stores domains, a campaign agent stores Meta campaign IDs, a concept agent stores concept tags). Rather than 8 different tables, we use one filter_payload jsonb column with per-agent schema validation in the application layer. This keeps adding new agents to a single migration. subscriptions One row per active digest subscription. The core table. Field Type Note id uuid PK Primary key client_id uuid FK References clients table agent_type enum daily_brief, weekly_goals, pacing, concept_monitor, campaign_monitor, lp_monitor, top_spend, competitor_daily filter_payload jsonb Agent-specific config (campaign_id, concept_name, url_pattern, competitor_list, etc.) delivery_channels text[] email, slack, in_app recipient_emails text[] Who gets the digest slack_channel_id text Optional Slack destination delivery_time_local time Default 08:00 client_timezone text America/Bogota, etc. status enum active, paused, cancelled next_run_at timestamptz Computed from delivery_time + tz digest_runs One row per digest delivery. Audit trail + chat context source. Field Type Note id uuid PK subscription_id uuid FK run_date date The reporting date metrics_snapshot jsonb Raw data pulled — used for chat context digest_text text Final markdown output sent to client digest_html text Email-ready HTML version claude_prompt_used text For debugging / audit claude_model text claude-opus-4-7, etc. delivery_status jsonb { email: "sent", slack: "sent" } chat_session_token uuid Pre-generated token for chat handoff agent_targets Subscriptions → trackable entities. Lets one client track 5 competitors with one subscription row. Field Type Note id uuid PK subscription_id uuid FK target_type enum campaign, concept, landing_page, competitor_domain, ad_filter target_id text Meta campaign_id, concept_id, URL, domain, etc. target_label text Human-readable label target_metadata jsonb Extra config — e.g. competitor display name kpi_definitions Per-client KPI definitions for the daily brief and goals tracking. Field Type Note id uuid PK client_id uuid FK kpi_key text spend, roas, cpa, ctr, cvr, etc. display_name text "Cost per acquisition" unit text $, %, x, count goal_value numeric Weekly target goal_direction enum maximize, minimize, hit_target chat_sessions When a client clicks "chat for details," this row is hydrated with the digest context. Field Type Note id uuid PK digest_run_id uuid FK session_token uuid Matches digest_runs.chat_session_token hydrated_context jsonb Full metrics snapshot + digest text loaded as system context conversation_log jsonb Messages array expires_at timestamptz 7 days from creation 03.02 — Example Filter Payloads // agent_type = 'campaign_monitor' { "campaign_ids": ["120210000123456789"], "metrics": ["spend", "roas", "cpa", "ctr", "frequency", "results"], "alert_thresholds": { "roas_below": 1.5, "cpa_above": 45 } } // agent_type = 'concept_monitor' { "concept_tags": ["UGC-testimonial", "founder-PAS"], "concept_match_mode": "any", // any | all "metrics": ["spend", "impressions", "ctr", "cpa", "roas", "video_3s"] } // agent_type = 'lp_monitor' { "url_filters": [ { "type": "campaign", "value": "120210000123456789" }, { "type": "ad_keyword", "value": "summer-sale-v3" } ], "metrics": ["sessions", "cvr", "bounce", "time_on_page", "scroll_depth", "cpa"] } // agent_type = 'competitor_daily' { "competitors": [ { "domain": "rivalbrand.com", "label": "Rival Brand", "fb_page_id": "123" }, { "domain": "competitor2.com", "label": "Competitor Two", "fb_page_id": "456" } ], "track": ["new_ads", "new_lps", "new_offers", "new_hooks", "new_scripts"] } 04.01 — The Five-Phase Lifecycle Every agent — regardless of type — follows the same five phases. This is the framework's contract. New agent types only have to ...

pages.title: Saints Label — Google Ads Assessment
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: Saints Label — Google Ads Assessment 90-day analysis window · Feb 1 to May 21, 2026 00 Contents What This Covers Google Ads assessment for Saints Label, built on 90 days of TripleWhale and in-platform data. Findings, the constraint that limits scale, and the first 30 days of work. 01 Business-Wide Context 02 ncROAS by Google Channel 03 Monthly ncROAS by Google 04 Demand Gen 05 Performance Max 06 Brand Search 07 Non-Branded Search 08 Shopping 09 Tracking & Account Controls 10 Primary Constraint 11 Path Forward 12 For the Call 01 Business-Wide Context The business is short of the 1.8x ncROAS floor Across the last 90 days, business-wide ncROAS came in at 1.69x. That's the only place the 1.8x to 2.0x benchmark applies. Channel-level ncROAS numbers report each channel's attributed share of new customer revenue under a multi-touch model and cannot be read against the business benchmark in isolation. $2.55M Total paid spend (90 days) All paid channels combined 68,173 New customers 98% of all purchases 1.69x Business-wide ncROAS Short of the 1.8x floor by 0.11x $281K Revenue gap to 1.8x floor At current 90-day paid spend This audit looks at Google Ads specifically. The rest of the page uses channel-level ncROAS to compare Google channels to each other and over time. Those numbers are not benchmark comparisons. 02 ncROAS by Google Channel Inside Google, the spend goes to the wrong place Core Issue Coverage 86.5% of Google spend went to Demand Gen at 1.68x ncROAS. Brand Search earned 3.60x ncROAS on 3.6% of Google spend. The Google channel mix is putting the most budget behind the channel with the lowest attributed efficiency per dollar. Channel 90-day spend Share ncROAS Brand Search $4,091 3.6% 3.60x Demand Gen $98,156 86.5% 1.68x Performance Max $7,170 6.3% 1.36x Shopping $2,344 2.1% 0.58x NB Search $1,739 1.5% 0.26x Linear All attribution from TripleWhale, Feb 1 to May 21, 2026. New-customer revenue only. Each channel's ncROAS reflects its attributed share of new customer revenue under TripleWhale's Linear All model. Higher numbers mean a channel earns more new-customer credit per dollar of spend. The comparison is between Google channels, not against the 1.8x business benchmark. 03 Monthly ncROAS by Google Demand Gen broke when it scaled Core Issue Delivery Demand Gen held 1.92x ncROAS through March and April, then dropped to 1.47x in May as monthly spend scaled to $52K. The drop coincides with budget growth, not with any external change. The channel is breaking under scale, not under demand. Monthly ncROAS by channel · Linear All attribution · Feb 1 to May 21, 2026 5x 4x 3x 2x 1x 0x 3.69x 3.36x 3.58x 4.62x 1.92x 1.92x 1.47x 0.28x 0.93x 2.12x Feb 2026 Mar 2026 Apr 2026 May 2026 Brand Search Demand Gen PMax Brand Search Held 3.36x to 4.62x ncROAS through every month at $362 to $1,794 of monthly spend. Spend fell while ncROAS stayed strong. The channel is under-funded, not under-performing. Demand Gen Stable through April at 1.92x ncROAS. Broke to 1.47x in May as spend hit $52K. The 22-campaign structure cannot absorb scale without losing signal efficiency. Performance Max 0.28x to 0.93x to 2.12x. The trajectory is positive. The campaign is learning and improving, but the recent 63 changes in 30 days are slowing the learning rate. 04 Demand Gen Demand Gen Core Issue Delivery 22 active Demand Gen campaigns. 18 of them are below Google's 50-conversion learning threshold. $13.9K of monthly Demand Gen spend is running in campaigns the algorithm cannot optimize. The May ncROAS drop from 1.92x to 1.47x is the structural problem showing up in the numbers. Analysis Each new creative batch launches as a new campaign instead of as an ad inside a consolidated campaign. At $50 to $300 daily budgets across 47 lifetime campaigns, conversion volume per campaign sits between 0 and 3 per day. That is below the threshold Maximize Conversions needs to learn cleanly. Every new batch starts the model from zero. 21 of the 22 active Demand Gen campaigns run on Maximize Conversions, not value-based bidding. The account optimizes for transaction count, ignoring revenue, despite a ROAS-targeted business goal. When monthly Demand Gen spend ramped from $7.9K in March to $52K in May, ncROAS dropped from 1.92x to 1.47x. The model gets weaker signal per dollar as budget spreads thinner across more campaigns sitting below the learning threshold. Recommendations Consolidate 22 campaigns into roughly 4, grouped by creative theme. Future creative batches launch as ads inside those campaigns, not as new campaigns. Move the consolidated campaigns to Maximize Conversion Value with a tROAS target tied to product margin. Reallocate freed budget toward Brand Search and Performance Max while Demand Gen restructures. 22 active Demand Gen campaigns, last 30 days 4 above threshold 50 or more conversions in the last 30 days 18 below threshold $13.9K of monthly Demand Gen spend Bid strategy split 21 of 22 active Demand Gen campaigns run on Maximize Conversions. 1 uses value-based bidding. 05 Performance Max Performance Max Core Issue Coverage + Delivery Performance Max ncROAS climbed from 0.28x to 0.93x to 2.12x across March, April, and May as the campaign learned. 64% of Performance Max spend is delivering on Google Search, returning $7,423 of attributed value at $4,584 of cost. The campaign is improving and is being held back by roughly 63 changes in the last 30 days. Analysis The search-terms report confirms Performance Max is capturing real non-branded category demand: "bible study guide" (414 clicks, 35 conversions, 8.45% conversion rate), "bible study guides", "66 page bible study guide", "bible study guides book". The branded queries that do appear (saintslabel.com, faith sprouts the 66 roots journey) are correctly excluded by the negative list. Branded delivery is not happening on this campaign. Performance Max is functioning as the de facto non-branded Search engine. It has to do that job without a dedicated Search campaign feeding it Quality Score signal, controlling intent tiers, or absorbing exact-match traffic. The campaign also has roughly 63 changes logged in 30 days, including repeated tROAS step-downs visible in the campaign name (2.8x then 2.5x then 2.7x). Value-based bidding strategies need around 14 days of stable signal to optimize. Every target change resets that learning. Recommendations Lock the tROAS target. Pick one number based on product margin and hold it for a full 14-day cycle before reviewing. Lift Performance Max budget as the learning trajectory continues. ncROAS doubled from April to May, and the campaign has not yet stabilized. Treat Performance Max as the Shopping and YouTube engine. Let a restructured Non-Branded Search campaign capture exact-match Search intent. pages.title: The Seven Layers of Alignment
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: The Seven Layers of Alignment Visual exploration · Internal VISUAL STUDY · 06 TREATMENTS The Seven Layers of Alignment A study of nested selves — from the body outward to the infinite. Six visual treatments, each carrying a different argument about how alignment works and where intervention happens. 01 Stratosphere 02 Ripples 03 Iceberg 04 Toroidal + Sketches FIG. 01 / STRATIFIED MODEL The Stratosphere Geological · Vertical · Gross to subtle A cross-section of self. The body is the bedrock; the digital is the ionosphere. Each layer rests on the one beneath. Misalignment is geological — slow, structural, and felt long before it's seen. FIG. 01 What this sells That alignment is foundational . A misaligned body cannot support an aligned spirit. A misaligned spirit cannot project coherently into the digital. The stack metaphor makes intervention obvious: start where the crack is, not where the symptom is. When to use it Best when arguing for sequence — that someone can't skip layers. Echoes Dilts' logical levels and the OSI model. Reads top-down or bottom-up; both directions tell a story. FIG. 02 / RADIAL MODEL Ripples Outward Concentric · Radial · Self at center Drop a pebble in water. The body is the pebble; each layer is the next wave. The digital is the ripple still moving long after you can no longer see it. FIG. 02 What this sells That alignment propagates . What happens at the Physical layer doesn't stay there — it becomes Emotional, Psychological, and eventually shows up Digitally. The ripple implies the source is small and the effect is vast. When to use it Best when arguing that inner work has external consequences . Echoes Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems and Hierocles' Circles of Concern. Strong for showing why personal practice matters at scale. FIG. 03 / VISIBILITY MODEL The Iceberg Visible / Hidden · What shows · What runs Most of what determines you sits beneath the waterline. The Physical, Relational, Environmental, and Digital are visible. The Emotional, Psychological, and Spiritual are not — and yet they steer everything above. FIG. 03 What this sells That what's online is downstream of what's interior . You can't fix your digital presence by editing your digital presence. The fix lives below the surface. The iceberg makes this visceral. When to use it Best when arguing against surface-level fixes. Especially powerful for a digital-native audience that lives at the top and forgets the bottom exists. Echoes the classic Hemingway iceberg theory. FIG. 04 / CIRCULATORY MODEL Toroidal Flow Circulation · Energy · Alignment as flow Energy rises from Physical, through the inner three, out through the outer three, into the Digital — and loops back. Alignment is circulation. Misalignment is blockage. FIG. 04 What this sells That alignment is dynamic, not static . The layers aren't shelves you check off — they're a system that has to keep moving. When one layer is blocked, the whole loop suffers. Closest in spirit to chakras and the kosha onion. When to use it Best when your audience is somatically literate — open to language like "energy" and "flow." The most spiritually-coded of the four. Could feel powerful or could feel woo, depending on the audience. FIG. + / EXPERIMENTAL TREATMENTS Further Sketches Experimental · Less polished · More provocative Six additional treatments worth considering. Some are stronger metaphors; some are stronger diagrams. Each prioritizes a different aspect of the model. SKETCH A The Matryoshka Nested dolls · each contains the next A nesting doll metaphor. Each layer literally contains the one beneath. Sells the idea that the inner self is preserved inside every outer expression — and that no layer is left behind. SKETCH B The Density Spectrum Gross to subtle · matter to information Physical DENSE Emotional Psychological Spiritual Relational Environmental Digital SUBTLE A logarithmic gradient from dense (physical) to subtle (digital). Borrowed from the Pancha Koshas. Makes the case that the Digital isn't less real — just less dense. Most defensible philosophically. SKETCH C The Constellation Network · non-hierarchical · interdependent Drops the hierarchy. Treats the 7 layers as nodes in a constellation, each pulling on the others. Useful when arguing that no layer is more important — alignment is the geometry between them. SKETCH D The Climbing Ladder Sequential · progressive · maturity arc Strictly ordered. Each layer is a rung; you can't skip. Borrows from Maslow and Dilts. Best when teaching the model as a developmental sequence — where are you currently spending most of your attention? SKETCH E The Scale of Being Editorial · printable · reference card A clean, printable reference. No metaphor, no embellishment — just the 7 layers labeled and ordered with subtitles. Strongest format for a one-pager, a wall print, or the back of a card. SKETCH F The Solar System Orbital · gravitational · self at center Body is the sun. Each layer orbits at greater radius. Digital is the outer planet — distant, vast, but still gravitationally bound to the core. Implies the inner self exerts pull on the outer layers, not the reverse.

pages.text: TTS Creator Recruitment SOP Ad Pros × Luhxe — TikTok Shop Creator Program Overview & Pipeline Math Finding Creator Emails Outreach System DM & Email Templates Onboarding & Activation Tool Stack & Budget YouTube Meta Playbook Program Overview Recruit 50 active TikTok Shop affiliate creators for Luhxe, a premium carry-on travel bag brand that has sold 100K+ units and runs approximately $2M/month in ad spend. Creators are compensated on a performance-based model: $150/month guaranteed base pay plus 3% of ad spend allocated to their content. 50 Active Creator Target $150 Monthly Guaranteed Base 3% Ad Spend Commission $2M Monthly Ad Spend Pipeline Math Expect approximately 10x pipeline to hit the 50-creator target. At each stage, conversion filters down: Stage Volume Conversion Notes Creators Identified 1,000 — Scraped / sourced across all channels Contacted (DM + Email) 500 50% Valid contact info found Responded 100–150 20–30% Cold DM 10–20%, email 25–35% Interested / Applied 75 50–75% $150 base converts fence-sitters Onboarded 60 80% Complete profile + first video Active (30-day retention) 50 83% Posting consistently Creator Earning Potential At $2M/month total ad spend, here's what a creator needs to earn at each tier: Monthly Goal Ad Spend on Their Content % of Total Spend Breakdown $500/mo $11,667 0.6% $150 base + $350 commission $1,000/mo $28,333 1.4% $150 base + $850 commission $1,500/mo $45,000 2.3% $150 base + $1,350 commission $2,000/mo $61,667 3.1% $150 base + $1,850 commission Key differentiator: The $150/month guaranteed base is what separates Luhxe from every other commission-only TTS program. Most brands offer 15–20% commission with zero floor. The guaranteed income is the line that stops the scroll in a creator's inbox. Source Channels (Priority Order) Layer these channels from warmest to coldest. Start with existing relationships and expand outward. 1 Luhxe's Existing Organic Creators Search TikTok for existing Luhxe UGC — anyone who has already tagged or mentioned the brand. These are the warmest leads with the highest conversion rate. Pull their profiles, check if they're TTS-enabled, and reach out directly. Expected yield: 10–30 warm leads. Conversion rate 50–70% (they already love the product). 2 TikTok Shop Affiliate Marketplace Use TikTok's built-in affiliate marketplace to find creators already selling in the travel, fashion, and lifestyle categories. Filter by GMV, follower count, and engagement rate. Invite directly through the platform. 3 TikTok Creator Marketplace (TTCM) Official TikTok platform for brand–creator partnerships. Advanced filters for audience demographics, content performance, and engagement metrics. Send collaboration invitations directly. 4 Competitor Creator Poaching via Analytics Tools Multiple analytics platforms track which creators are promoting which products on TikTok Shop. Use these to identify proven performers selling competitor products (Away, Béis, Monos, July, Samsonite). Tool Key Feature Pricing Best For Kalodata Product-level creator tracking, GMV estimates, top seller rankings $59–$199/mo Identifying high-GMV creators on competitor products FastMoss 250M+ creator profiles, exports up to 6K contacts/day, revenue overlays $99–$299/mo Bulk export of competitor creator lists with contact data EchoTik Chrome extension overlaying revenue data as you browse TikTok ~$9/mo Real-time scouting while browsing — see revenue per creator Competitor Swipe workflow: Search competitor product → sort creators by GMV → export contact list → pitch with money-driven angle: "You're already selling travel bags. Our creators earn $150/mo guaranteed + 3% of ad spend. Want in?" 5 Instagram / YouTube Cross-Platform Sourcing Many TikTok creators also post on Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Search travel and packing content on those platforms, find creators with TikTok presence, and cross-reference. 6 Scraping Tools for Email Extraction Use IGLeads or similar tools to bulk-scrape emails from TikTok/Instagram bios. Always verify emails with NeverBounce or ZeroBounce before sending to maintain deliverability. 7 Off-Platform Communities Recruit from Discord servers, Facebook Groups, and Reddit communities focused on TikTok Shop selling, UGC creation, and influencer marketing. These creators are actively looking for brand deals. Outreach Cadence A structured multi-touch sequence across DM and email. Day 5 and Day 10 follow-ups significantly increase response rates. pages.text: TurboTax Live's $2B Business, Decoded Business model & unit economics deep dive • April 2026 How TurboTax Live scaled to $2.0 billion A hybrid software + human expert model that cracked the $35B assisted tax market — growing 47% in a single year while maintaining 74%+ segment operating margins. $2.0B FY2025 TT Live Revenue 47% YoY Revenue Growth 24% Customer Growth 15K W-2 Tax Experts The Hybrid Model TurboTax Live combines TurboTax's DIY software with on-demand access to credentialed human tax experts (CPAs and Enrolled Agents), delivered virtually. The product exists in two tiers targeting fundamentally different customer needs. Expert Assist (rebranded from "Live Assisted" for the 2026 tax season) lets customers prepare their own returns using TurboTax software while accessing unlimited on-demand help from tax experts via phone, chat, or one-way video. Every Expert Assist return receives a final comprehensive review by a human expert before filing. This tier targets the "anxious DIY filer." Expert Full Service (rebranded from "Live Full Service") is a complete handoff: a matched tax expert prepares, reviews, signs, and files the entire return. The customer uploads documents, meets virtually (or in-person at one of approximately 600 expert offices and 20 branded TurboTax storefronts ), reviews the completed return, and approves filing. This tier directly competes with H&R Block, Jackson Hewitt, and local CPA firms — the $35 billion assisted tax preparation market encompassing roughly 85 million professionally prepared returns annually. Key insight: TurboTax Live sits inside Intuit's Consumer Group segment, which generated $4.87B in FY2025 . TT Live's $2.0B represents 41% of Consumer Group revenue — up from ~30% a year earlier — and Intuit's CFO has stated it will become the majority of Consumer Group revenue in the coming years. Revenue Math: 39M Returns & Rising ARPR Total TurboTax returns filed were approximately 39.2 million in FY2025 — actually declining 2% YoY. This is a deliberate choice : Intuit has pursued shedding low-value customers to increase average revenue per return. "Pay-nothing" customers dropped from over 10M in FY2023 to roughly 8M in FY2025. Meanwhile, online paying units grew 6% and ARPR increased approximately 13%. The ARPR differential between DIY and Live is stark. A blended DIY customer generates roughly $50–90 . A TurboTax Live customer generates an estimated $200–250 — approximately 3–4x the DIY average . Metric FY2023 FY2024 FY2025 Consumer Group Revenue $4.14B $4.45B $4.87B TurboTax Live Revenue ~$1.17B ~$1.33B $2.00B TT Live % of Consumer ~28% ~30% 41% TT Live Revenue Growth 17% 17% 47% TT Live Customer Growth 12% 11% 24% ARPR Growth — — ~13% Total TurboTax Returns ~40.3M 39.9M 39.2M Unit Economics: W-2 Experts & AI Cost Compression The cost structure of TurboTax Live differs fundamentally from DIY TurboTax, which is essentially pure software with near-zero marginal cost and estimated gross margins of 90–95% . TurboTax Live introduces human labor as a significant cost component. Intuit employs approximately 15,000 tax experts as W-2 employees , not 1099 contractors. Average compensation runs approximately $40/hour ($83K annualized), with CPA-credentialed Full Service experts earning around $54/hour ($112K annualized). Fully loaded with benefits and overhead (30–40% burden rate), the effective cost per expert hour runs $52–70 . Tier Avg. Expert Time Est. Labor Cost/Customer Est. Gross Margin Expert Assist 15–30 min $20–50 60–75% Expert Full Service 1.5–2 hrs $80–140 40–55% Blended TT Live — — 50–65% DIY TurboTax (comparison) 0 min ~$0 90–95% Seasonal workforce management is central to viability. Tax experts work primarily January through April, with shifts of 4+ hours during a 5 AM–9 PM PT window, seven days per week. Intuit Academy (which has trained over 129,000 learners) serves as both a recruiting funnel and upskilling platform. Rehires return without re-interviewing. Pricing Architecture & Upsell Mechanics Tier DIY (Federal) Expert Assist (Federal) Expert Full Service (Federal) Basic / Simple Free $79 Starting $129 Deluxe $79 $139 Forms-based Premium $139 $209 Up to $409+ State Filing $0–$64 $59–$69 $69 The price premium for Expert Assist over DIY ranges from $60–79 at equivalent complexity levels. Expert Full Service uses forms-based pricing that scales with return complexity — aligning cost-to-serve with revenue per return. Intuit's upsell mechanics begin before a customer selects a product. The landing experience uses a quiz-based recommendation system that typically defaults to recommending Expert Assist. Complexity triggers (investment income, self-employment, itemized deductions) force mandatory upgrades to paid tiers. The "start free, pay when you file" model creates significant sunk-cost friction. Additional revenue extraction includes a $40 refund processing fee , audit defense add-ons, MAX protection packages, and Refund Advance loans that drive Credit Karma Money account openings. The "Beat Your Price" guarantee (10% savings vs. previous tax preparer) directly targets H&R Block and CPA client conversion. Growth Arc: $0 → $1B → $2B TurboTax Live traces its origins to SmartLook (January 2016). The product officially launched in November 2017 . When Sasan Goodarzi became CEO in January 2019, he made TurboTax Live central to his vision of transforming Intuit into an "AI-driven expert platform." The Full Service tier launched in December 2020 , marking the critical expansion from "help me do my taxes" to "do my taxes for me." Full Service customers more than tripled in FY2022, the same year TurboTax Live crossed the $1 billion revenue threshold . Three levers drove the jump from ~$1.3B to $2.0B in a single year: Customer volume surged 24% — fueled by Credit Karma integration (3x higher TurboTax starts, zero-click login rates from 5% to 70%), 600 expert offices, and the Beat Your Price offer ARPR expanded ~13% — through mix shift toward higher-priced Full Service and faster-refund-access features AI-driven productivity gains — serving 24% more customers without proportionally scaling the 15,000-expert workforce Early FY2026 signal: Q1 FY2026 (ending October 2025) showed TurboTax Live revenue growing 51% year-over-year , suggesting the acceleration is continuing. AI Is Rewriting the Margin Equation Intuit Assist — built on the proprietary GenOS system using a hybrid architecture of Anthropic Claude and OpenAI GPT models — is fundamentally reshaping TurboTax Live's unit economics. 20% Less Expert Time per Return 90% Tax Forms Auto-Processed $90M Annualized AI Efficiencies (H1 FY25) 12% Faster Customer Filing Time AI enables an "AI-first, human-escalation" model where Intuit Assist handles routine questions and pre-call preparation, while human experts focus on complex judgment calls. Each expert can serve more customers per hour — the key to scaling a 15,000-person workforce to serve millions of Live customers. Intuit's roadmap points toward agentic AI — autonomous AI agents for customer service, payment processing, and tax preparation that communicate with each other and escalate to humans only when necessary. The long-term trajectory appears aimed at approaching DIY-like margins on assisted products by minimizing — though never eliminating — the human touch. Path to $3B+ : The Key Levers The $2.0 billion FY2025 milestone is standalone TurboTax Live revenue , not a blended segment figure. It was reached through a three-part formula: aggressive customer acquisition (24% growth), rising ARPR (13%), and AI-compressed cost-to-serve (20% expert time reduction). The path forward hinges on three structural advantages: $35 billion TAM — TurboTax Live has barely penetrated the ~85M returns currently done by traditional preparers. pages.text: ad pros Factory · Rev 3.5 01 Overview 02 The Loop 03 Agents 04 Sequence 05 Gates 06 Foundation 07 Build Your Own Autonomous Workflow Factory · 100+ Workflows The factory recommends, designs, and deploys every workflow inside the 8-step flow. The LTV analysis is one workflow. Ad Pros needs 100 of them — creative audits, media reallocations, churn investigations, launches, retros. Humans can't author each one by hand, and humans shouldn't even be the ones deciding which ones to build next. This is the factory: agents recommending agents, agents designing agents, agents deploying agents — with three human gates during design and zero during development. 8 Factory agents — including a Recommender that decides what to build next 3 Human gates — Brief, Blueprint, Skills. Everything else autonomous. ~ 4 hr Request to deployed workflow, wall-clock 100+ Target workflow library within 12 months The Core Insight The factory is itself an instance of the 8-step flow — and it's self-directing . Every workflow Ad Pros produces follows Collect → Organize → Remember → Think → Plan → Do → Review → Improve . The factory is no different. But the real breakthrough isn't just that the factory builds workflows — it's that the factory decides which workflows to build next . When existing workflows run, the Improve Agent sees where humans kept editing briefs, which clients kept asking for new analyses, which gaps the current library can't fill . It feeds those signals to the Recommender Agent , which proposes the next workflow to build. Humans approve the queue — they don't invent it. This is what makes it autonomous: the factory's backlog is written by the factory itself. Every workflow shipped teaches the factory to ship the next one better and to know what to ship next. That compounding loop is the whole bet. 02 · The Autonomous Loop Signals in. Workflows out. Feedback back in. This is the design flow for autonomous agent creation. The Recommender Agent kicks it off not because a human asked, but because the factory's own observations flagged a gap. Human gates only enforce quality at three design moments. The self-directing factory loop Agents → Agents → Agents ◉ Phase 1 · Signals What does Ad Pros need next? The Recommender Agent watches every deployed workflow + every client signal + every gap the Improve Agent surfaces. Proposes the next workflow to build. RECOMMENDER IMPROVE → ◉ Phase 2 · Factory How does it get designed ? Six specialist agents run in parallel + sequence to produce the Blueprint, Skills, and Eval harness. Three human gates enforce quality. INTAKE SHAPE STAGE ×11 SKILLS EVAL → ◉ Phase 3 · Deploy How does it ship ? The Deploy Agent builds the ClickUp workflow end-to-end: List, custom fields, tasks, dependencies, Autopilot Agents, saved template. Fully idempotent. DEPLOY ↺ Feedback loop: every deployed workflow's run data flows back to the Improve Agent → Recommender Agent. The factory's own outputs write the factory's next backlog item. This is what makes it autonomous: the signal-to-build loop doesn't require a human to initiate. Mapped to the 8-step Intelligence Flow Factory activity per stage 01 Collect What's happening? REC INT 02 Organize Where does it go? SHP 03 Remember What do we know? SKL 04 Think What do we do? STG 05 Plan How do we do it? STG EVL 06 Do Who does what? DEP 07 Review Did it work? EVL 08 Improve What changes? IMP REC 03 · The Eight Factory Agents Not generic meta-agents. Factory workers with specific jobs. Each agent has a single job, a narrow output, and a clear hand-off. The Recommender opens the loop. The Improve Agent closes it. The six in between do the design work. Three gates enforce quality. ◉ Roster · Tap an agent to jump to full card 8 agents 01 The Recommender Agent Decides what workflow to build next — watches signals, proposes ranked backlog. NEW Collect Auto 02 The Intake Agent Parses the request — expands approved items into a structured Workflow Brief. Collect Gate 1 03 The Shape Agent Picks the skeleton — one of 8 canonical shapes, tagged read- or write-heavy. Organize Auto 04 The Stage Designer (×11) Designs the insides — 11 parallel agents, one per stage; Blueprint Merger joins. Think Gate 2 Parallel 05 The Skills Curator Maps the Skills — reuses library first, drafts new SKILL.md only when needed. Remember Gate 3 06 The Eval Agent Gates deployment — generates test suite, assertions, anti-hacking scans. Review Auto 07 The Deploy Agent Builds it in ClickUp — List, tasks, dependencies, Autopilot Agents, template. Do Auto 08 The Improve Agent Closes the loop — reflects on runs, rewrites factory prompts, feeds Recommender. Improve Auto 01 The Recommender Agent The Recommender Agent NEW · Opens the loop Step 01 — Collect Autonomous The most important agent — because it removes the human from the "what should we build next?" decision. Watches deployed workflow performance, client signals, Improve Agent patterns, and the Skills Library's gaps. Proposes the next workflow to add to the queue. Writes a ranked backlog with justification per item. Without this agent, the factory still needs a human to decide what to build. With it, the factory is genuinely self-directing — humans approve the queue, but agents populate it. pages.title: The STARR Yap Method
pages.author: Adrienne Dyer
pages.text: The STARR Yap Method A 5-beat structure for short-form talking-head videos · Reverse-engineered from a viral teardown Transcript & SOP Best Practices Research Source Video · 60s · @founder reel I cracked yap content. A creator built a 5-beat structure he calls the STARR method — a repeatable framework for short-form, talking-head ("yap") videos that hold attention and convert. Reverse-engineered below into a shoot-ready SOP for any Ad Pros founder, AI twin, or creator-network partner shipping daily reels. Transcript Reconstructed from burned-in captions plus the on-screen STARR graphic. Mid-section voiceover (0:13–0:48) was delivered over a framework reveal with no captions; the spoken letters mapped 1:1 to the on-screen build. 0:00–0:05 "The rumors are true — I've solved yapping." 0:06–0:12 "It took me 250 videos studying [this], but everyone's using…" 0:13–0:48 [STARR framework graphic builds letter-by-letter, in sync with VO. Each letter is named, defined, then crossed off as the next one fills in.] S Shocking T Text Hook A Achievement R Roadmap R Recipe 0:49–0:57 "This video has used all five points of the STARR method, and this is how you can yap like a pro." 0:58–1:00 "Follow for more. Bye." [wave + cut] SOP — The STARR Method Use this 5-beat structure for any solo, camera-direct Reel/TikTok/Short where a founder or creator is talking to camera. Best for 45–60s clips. Each letter = one specific job. Cut the video into the same 5 beats and you've got the structure. S Shocking Open with a claim that stops the scroll. Lead with the punchline, not the setup. Frame as a result, a contradiction, or a "rumors are true" reveal. The first 1.5 seconds decides whether the rest of your video gets watched. "The rumors are true — I've solved yapping." T Text Hook Persistent on-screen title that reinforces the promise visually. Stays on screen the full duration. Black pill or yellow accent, top-center, max 5–7 words. A subhead in parentheses sharpens the angle. Carries the message for the 80%+ of viewers watching with sound off. "I CRACKED YAP CONTENT (New Viral Yap Method)" A Achievement One sentence of credibility — why should they keep watching you . Quantify effort or outcome (volume, reps, results). Don't list credentials, cite the work. Specific is sticky; vague is skippable. "It took me 250 videos studying this." R Roadmap Tell them exactly what they're about to learn. Name the framework. Use an acronym or numbered list — gives the viewer a finish line so they stay till the end. Reveal the structure visually (animated framework card) as you say it. The framework name is the retention tool. "I'm going to show you the 5-letter STARR method." R Recipe Walk through each step concretely. The "how." One letter at a time, fill in the framework graphic in sync with the voiceover. Each letter = one specific, copyable instruction. Close by pointing at the video itself as proof: "this video used all five — that's how you yap like a pro." Reveal letter → define → cross off → reveal next. Self-referential close.
